articleTitle: Low sidelobe leaky wave antenna based on gap waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a novel low sidelobe leaky wave antenna (LWA) using groove gap waveguide (GGW) technology for Ku band is presented. The low sidelobe character is achieved by setting the different height of mental pins on one side of the GGW to control the leakage rate of the antenna. The impedance bandwidth of this antenna is from 13.5 GHz to 17.5 GHz with an average gain around 18dBi. Moreover, the sidelobe level is below -21.8dB and the beam directions range from 23.9° to 47.7°.

articleTitle: SIW circularly-polarized filtering antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a new design of planar circularly-polarized (CP) filtering antenna using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavities is presented. The design is based on the dual-mode cavity structure using TE120 and TE210 modes. The satisfying filtering performance of the antenna is realized by a coupled-resonator circuit of the two SIW cavities. And the radiating element is a non-uniform ring slot integrated with the output cavity to form a cavity-backed CP ring-slot antenna. Commercial software package ANSYS HFSS is used to simulate this antenna. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna can provide both the reasonable good filtering and CP radiating performances simultaneously.

articleTitle: Endfire antennas based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A linear polarized (LP) endfire antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) is proposed, which is composed of a feed monopole and ultrathin corrugated metallic strips. The metallic strips are utilized to couple guided wave into SSPP, propagate SSPP, and radiate the SSPP into free space. As an example, an X-band prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured. Both the simulated and measured results show good agreement, and verify that the proposed antenna behaves good performances. Similar to travelling wave antennas, gain of the proposed antenna is in proportional to the length of the strips structure. Furthermore, a circular polarized (CP) endfire antenna is also designed by arranging two LP antennas with different strip height in orthogonal. The simulated results verify our prediction.

articleTitle: Shaping optimization of double reflector antenna based on manifold mapping
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, two methods of analyzing the double reflector antenna are introduced: the physical optics method (PO) and the shooting and bouncing rays method (SBR). In the process of optimizing the design of reflector antenna, in order to accelerate the calculation speed of the optimization, this paper uses manifold mapping to assist the operation, significantly improving computing speed. Manifold mapping algorithm divides the structures requiring optimization into two models, namely a coarse model with low simulation precision and less time-consuming and a fine model with high simulation precision but more time-consuming. In this paper we use the PO as a fine model and SBR as a coarse model. Reflector antenna is optimized by the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize the antenna pattern which covers a specific area.

articleTitle: A wideband CP millimeter wave antenna by using 3D printed technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a new technology to realize a millimeter wave antenna with circular polarization. The antenna has a complex structure which consists of several dielectric slabs to achieve wideband, high-gain performance. Thank to the 3D printing technologies, the complex antenna can be easily fabricated with low cost. The proposed antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth of 50% from 45 to 75 GHz for the VSWR ≤ 2, and yields an overlapped axial ratio bandwidth of 37% from 46 to 67 GHz for the axial ratio ≤ 3 dB. The maximum gain of the antenna reaches to 15 dBic. The proposed work is simple in design, easy for fabrication, and with noticeable electrical characteristics.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional DOA estimation with reduced-dimension MUSIC algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This letter discusses the problem of Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation for two-dimension antenna array, and derives a reduced-dimension multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm therein. The proposed algorithm, which only requires one dimension search, can avoid the high computational cost within two-dimension MUSIC (2D-MUSIC) algorithm. We illustrate that the algorithm has very close performance to 2D-MUSIC algorithm without an accurate number of signals. Simulation results verify the usefulness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Waveform of class E power amplifiers with PI network
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the waveform of the class E power amplifier with pi network in the time domain is analyzed. The analytical design expressions are derived and the effects of series inductance on the waveform are obtained compared with conventional topology. The results suggest that this new topology can obtain high power output capability Cp in broadband. The maximum of the power output capability is equal to 0.1049.

articleTitle: Chipless graphene tag and dual-CP reader for Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a printable chipless tag that encodes more bits than a conventional tag, and also a dual circularly polarized (CP) reader that achieves high isolation as well as insensitive orientation. To demonstrate this concept, a radio-frequency identification (RFID) tag with a compact size of 12mm × 12mm is designed to encode 8 bits covering 6-9 GHz, and is investigated with dual-CP backscattering characteristics. Using conductive ink such as graphene, it is possible to directly print this kind of chipless tag on A4 papers, clothes, plastics, etc. This flexible low-cost tag and dual-CP reader are promising to significantly benefit the Internet of Things (IoT).

articleTitle: Wide band wide scanning angle phased array antenna design in Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact wide band phased array antenna is presented. The proposed array antenna consists of 1024 elements providing wide band and wide scanning angle in Ku-band. The array antenna is fed by a microstripbalun printed on the bottom side of the dielectric substrate (Rogers RO3450 substrate, with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=3.66 and thickness of 0.508 mm), while a dipole with parasitic structures is placed on the top side of the same substrate. With this simple arrangement, a wide band design is realized for beam scanning angle of ±45° phased array antenna in Ku-band. Details of the proposed antenna design are described and simulated results are presented.

articleTitle: Simulation for several kinds of TEM horn antenna used by NEMP simulator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Aiming at improving the radiation direction of the radiating high altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse(NEMP) simulator, Transverse electromagnetic(TEM) horn antenna is adopted as the radiating antenna for the simulator in this paper. Several structures are simulated using the CST microwave studios software. Results suggest that TEM horn antenna can be used by NEMP simulators with some limitations; the near field waveform is closer to standard waveform than far field one; the structures of impedance loading and low frequency compensation have limited effect on improving the antenna's radiation performance; the other two structures of impedance with gradually exponential changing and edges rolling can perfect the radiation waveforms greatly.

articleTitle: A compact size dual-polarized high-gain resonant cavity antenna at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a compact size dual-polarized high-gain resonant cavity antenna (RCA) at 28 GHz is presented. The RCA consists of two layers of substrates. The upper layer is composed of a square patch-type frequency selective surface (FSS), a dual-polarized microstrip patch antenna fed by two coaxial SMA connectors is placed onto the lower substrate as the feeding system. The electromagnetic waves can be reflected inside the cavity continuously by adjusting the height of cavity. The gains of the microstrip patch antenna in orthogonal polarizations can be enhanced though the introduction of FSS as a partially reflective surface. The antenna has a compact size of 30 mm × 30 mm, however, the gains of two linear polarizations at 28 GHz can reach 17.3 dBi and 17.2 dBi, respectively. The -10 dB impedance bandwidth of both the two ports can reach 1.3 GHz from 27.3 GHz to 28.6 GHz.

articleTitle: A wideband gain enhancement and RCS reduction patch antenna using improved loading method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The simultaneous improvement of radiating and scattering performance of an antenna is normally considered as a contradiction. In this paper, wideband gain enhancement and radar cross section (RCS) reduction are both achieved for a conventional patch antenna by loading metamaterial in an improved way. Through a detailed investigation of loading manners, the proposed patch antenna with both improved RCS and gain is proposed and experimentally validated. Both simulated and measured results show that, compared to the original antenna, the gain of the proposed antenna is enhanced almost over the whole operation band, and the wideband (in-band and out-of-band) RCS reduction is achieved concurrently.

articleTitle: A persistent imaging method for video-SAR in terahertz band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Video-SAR is a new imaging mode, where the radar system enables continuous data collection and processes SAR imagery in rapid succession. Typically, the flight path of Video-SAR is circular and the radar beam provides continuous surveillance over a region of interest. Due to two drawbacks, the traditional PFA(Polar Format Algorithm) for circular SAR imaging is not particularly appropriate for Video-SAR frames. First, Video-SAR frames should be oriented in a fixed direction on the ground coordinate system (GCS), while the PFA forms the image frames on the sub-aperture coordinate system (SCS), which has a rotating angle to the GCS. Second, each sub-aperture overlaps with its adjacent ones to increasing the frame rate, and the repeated interpolation of the overlapped sub-apertures is needed when using the traditional PFA, which leads to reduce imaging efficiency. In this paper, we will show an improved PFA where the Video-SAR frames can be oriented in a fixed direction on GCS and the repeated interpolation is avoided in the overlaps. Finally, the effectiveness of the improved algorithm is verified by the experimental data collected by a THz Radar Systems.

articleTitle: Potential active shooter detection using a portable radar sensor with micro-Doppler and range-Doppler analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Micro-Doppler and range-Doppler provide useful information related to the movement of a human subject. This work demonstrates the feasibility of remotely identifying a potential active shooter with concealed weapon based on micro-Doppler and range-Doppler signatures. By studying and comparing micro-Doppler and range-Doppler information of human subjects carrying a concealed rifle versus other similar activities, special features of carrying a concealed rifle are identified, which can be applied to the detection of people with suspicious behaviors.

articleTitle: FDTD simulation of metasurfaces with generalized sheet transition conditions
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper simulates scattering properties of metasurfaces by finite difference time domain(FDTD) method with generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) to alleviate computational burden. It is found that a metasurface can be represented by the electric and magnetic polarization densities, which is related to electromagnetic field by GSTCs. The GSTCs are thereby implemented in 3D FDTD codes and the FDTD simulation of metasurfaces results agree well with simulated results from HFSS.

articleTitle: A shooting and bouncing ray method for dielectric media
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method for dielectric media is presented in this paper. The tracing rays are used to approximate the electromagnetic wave in this method. The transmission/reflection coefficients of the dielectric media are induced to calculate the attenuation during the propagation. The proposed algorithm is able to calculate the radar cross section (RCS) of dielectric media. Several numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of compact microstrip branchline couplers for broadband circularly polarized DRAs
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A systematic procedure for design of a broadband circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna (CP DRA) is presented. An important stage of this process is the design of a microstrip branchline coupler that realizes a required excitation of a particular dual-input CP DRA over the frequency range of interest. This excitation is developed to improve the axial ratio, otherwise degraded due to coupling between the dual inputs of the DRA. The designed branchline couplers have smaller footprint than corresponding quadrature hybrids. At the final stage, simulation-based tuning is applied to the entire CP DRA-feed structure to control several figures of interest, e.g., broadside AR, reflection coefficient, and total radiated power over the frequencies, as well as to account for coupling and parasitic radiation. An example of a 2.2 GHz cylindrical CP DRA illustrates our approach which, to our understanding, is also suitable for different types of dual-input CP antennas.

articleTitle: W-band longitudinal-slot coupling four-way SIW power combiner/divider
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel W-band four-way substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) power combiner/divider is analyzed and demonstrated. By combining a compact wideband antipodal fin-line transition configuration and the four-way longitudinal-slot SIW coupling structure, a novel back-to-back power dividing/ combining system is achieved, which can operate in the frequency band of 90.5-94.5 GHz with return loss of better than 12 dB and total insertion loss of less than 3.8 dB. Such power combiner/divider has advantages of high port-isolation, low insertion loss, high efficiency, wide band, and small lateral size, which is suitable for the spatial power amplifier applications.

articleTitle: Parameters estimation of mixed far-field and near-field sources via second order statistics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel algorithm for the joint estimation of DOA, range and frequency of mixed far-field and near-field sources. Based on the second order statistics of a symmetric uniform linear array, this method constructs two correlation matrices in the first step to obtain the estimates of DOA and frequency parameters. In the second step, two more correlation matrices are derived. The range and frequency values can be obtained in this step. The resultant algorithm has a low computational cost since it only requires second order statistics. Additionally, it avoids multi-dimensional spectral search. Simulation results are presented to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Location extraction of scattering center based on target surface currents
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a method to extract locations of sliding scattering centers of conducting streamlined target based on surface equivalent currents. To validate feasibility of this method, extracted results of two streamlined targets have been compared with the theoretical locations of the scattering centers. The comparison results show good agreement with each other.

articleTitle: Dual-polarization near-field focused reflective metasurface for WPT in X-band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new design of a dual-polarization near-field focused reflective metasurface for wireless power transfer. The reflective metasurface is composed of printed cross-dipole elements with different arm lengths, which is aimed to independently generate focused point with dual-polarization. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed reflective metasurface can focus the microwave power in the radiation near-field region to the desired focal points when illuminated by a feed horn. The wireless power transfer efficiency can achieve 77.3% at 10.2GHz and the bandwidth over 50% is from 9.6GHz to 11GHz. The proposed reflective metasurface has the great advantage of polarization independent, arbitrary position of focal points, high efficiency, which is suitable for wireless power transfer in radiating (Fresnel) near fields.

articleTitle: Analysis of deceptive moving target generated by single jammer in multi-channel SAR-GMTI
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Based on three-channel SAR-GMTI system, the velocity and location of the deceptive moving target generated by single jammer are studied. Study result shows that both the deceptive stationary target and moving target can be considered as moving target, and the estimated azimuth location which has nothing to do with the setting value is the same as jammer.

articleTitle: A dual-band monopole antenna for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel Dual band monopole WLAN antenna is proposed in this paper. The design idea of the antenna is derived from the dipole antenna. The size of proposed antenna is much smaller than that of conventional dipole antenna. Two antenna shaped L structure by rotating the radiation part of dipole antenna, so in the case of the dual band, the size of antenna can be reduced to no more than 0.7 wavelengths. The lumped port on the microstrip feed line structure is applied to feed the antenna. The reflection coefficient, radiation pattern and gain of the antenna is simulated and calculated. The simulation results are as follows: The high frequency and low frequency resonance frequencies of the frequency monopole antenna fall on the IEEE 802.11a (5.15~5.825GHz) and IEEE 802.11b (2.4~2.4825GHz) operating frequency bands, respectively, which is suitable for our requirements.

articleTitle: Low-cost two-layer terahertz transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A flat terahertz transmitarray with a two-layer element is investigated. The proposed element can provide 360° phase coverage with a transmission coefficient better than -3.52 dB at 250GHz. Then a transmitarray based on the element is designed with a low focal-to-diameter ratio of 0.3. Simulation results reveal that the transmitarray has large backward radiation. A WR-03 open-ended waveguide with a thick wall is used to feed the transmitarray, thus the backward radiation is further reflected to the forward direction and the gain is increased by 1.7 dB at 250GHz. Then the transmitarray is fabricated using standard, low-cost printed-circuit-board technology, and the measured results show that a peak gain of 28.8dBi with an aperture efficiency of 32% is achieved. In general, the proposed transmitarray has simple structures and can be fabricated by standard printed-circuit-board technologies which are suitable for applications in low-cost terahertz systems.

articleTitle: Sleep apnea detection with Doppler radar based on residual comparison method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to detect the obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) accurately, a non-contact way using Doppler radar is presented in this paper. The residual comparison based algorithm has been proposed to enhance the body movement cancellation and pre-event baseline calculation, so that the OSA event can be detected accurately. The experimental result shows the effectiveness of the proposed method for diagnosing the OSA event.

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for null broadending beamforming based on subspace projection and virtual antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a new algorithm to broaden the width of null is proposed. The algorithm is based on the property of subspace orthogonal principle between signal and noise and on virtual antenna array. Also diagonal loading technique is used to form robust beam pattern. With the theoretical analysis and computer simulations, it's shown that the superiority of proposed algorithm over other null broadening beamforming methods.

articleTitle: Sensitivity optimization of antenna for non-invasive blood glucose monitoring
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A microstrip ring antenna is optimized for non-invasive blood glucose monitoring. The main objective is to maximize the sensitivity of antenna w.r.t. the change of concentration of aqueous glucose solution. The parameterized antenna model and solution model are simulated in CST Microwave Studio in order to evaluate the sensitivity of the antenna design. The design process is implemented through a Matlab-CST socket. A maximum frequency shift of 85.5 MHz w.r.t. the range of the dielectric constant is obtained.

articleTitle: A 620–690 GHz sub-harmonic mixer based on monolithic GaAs integrated schottky diodes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a 620-690GHz sub-harmonic mixer using monolithic GaAs integrated schottky diodes is presented in order to remove the mismatch caused by manual assembly of the flip chip diode. The monolithic microwave integrated circuit integrates a Schottky anti-parallel diodes pair in a longitudinal configuration. We mostly analyzed the influence caused by diode position offset and conductive adhesive thickness on the performance of the mixer, which shows the necessity of monolithic integration technology. In 620GHz to 690 GHz simulated results of the mixer had achieved less than 9dB of conversion loss and 920K for DSB noise temperature within the bandwidth.

articleTitle: Ka band aperture-coupled patch antenna with stacked parasitic strips based on LTCC technology for circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a Ka-band aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna (ACMPA) based on low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology for circular polarization (CP) at 29 GHz. The antenna consists of an aperture coupled patch with stacked parasitic strips (SPS). The CP is produced by cutting the patch and the parasitic strips. The antenna provides an impedance bandwidth of 1.2 GHz from 28 GHz to 29.2 GHz with an axial ratio bandwidth of 3.8GHz from 26.6 to 30.4 GHz. The radiation patters are broad sided with a maximum gain of 7.29dBi.

articleTitle: Application of miniaturized indefinite magnetic metamaterial lens in wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The application of miniaturized indefinite magnetic metamaterial lens (IMML) in wireless power transfer (WPT) are numerically investigated. Vibrations of efficiency can be observed by sweeping the geometrical size or permeability of the IMML. By optimizing the parameters of IMML, the volume of the metamaterial lens can be miniaturized to the extent in which the lens is portable and flexible enough for practical using without obvious sacrifice of efficiency comparing to large-sized planar metamaterial lens. Furthermore, this phenomenon can be viewed as the performance of metamaterial resonator.

articleTitle: A compact broadband UHF RFID tag antenna for metallic objects
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a compact broadband RFID(radio frequency identification) tag antenna mountable on metallic object is proposed. The proposed antennas is contained two layers, a radiating patch with slots is printed on the upper dielectric substrate and the under dielectric substrate is surrounded by metal strap that with a slot. The input impedance of the antenna can be easily adjusted by changing slots dimensions. The antenna has compact size of 75mm×20mm×3mm and realized gain is about 3.3dBi. The simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth (reflection coefficient<;-10dB) is 197MHz(21.5%) from 795-992MHz. The measured identification distance is 3.8m.

articleTitle: A novel wideband frequency selective surface with dense arranged hybrid elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband frequency selective surface (FSS), which possesses the properties of flat response and stable performance. Y-loop is surrounded by cross-loops, which are distributed in a dense arrangement. The FSS is sandwiched by two dielectric layers. Simulation results show that this single-layer FSS, composed of hybrid elements, possesses a wide bandwidth of 13.65 GHz, and also a stable band-pass behavior. The fractional bandwidth reaches 54.3% at normal incidence.

articleTitle: A V-band SIW filter with transmission zero based on high-order mode coupling
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a fourth-order V-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter is presented. The design of this filter is based on high-order mode coupling. By adding two different over mode cavity coupling, two transmission zeros are generated at both side of the passband to get better out-of-band suppression. As demonstrations, the filter was processed using a RT/Duroid 5880 dielectric plate with a thickness of 0.254 mm. Good results between simulated and measured are obtained.

articleTitle: A novel stack PCB structure for X-band cavity bandpass filter implementation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel printed-circuit-board (PCB) structure is used to construct a 2nd-order annular cavity bandpass filter and a novel packaging technology are presented in this letter. The PCB has the treatment of shaped-cut, copper-deposition, and stack-management to generate the air cavity structure. A 2nd-order bandpass air-filled cavity filter with two transmission zeros at lower- and upper-stopband is designed, which has a central frequency at 9.88 GHz and a bandwidth of 1.8%. To validate the proposed concept, the proposed 2nd-order bandpass filter is fabricated. The measured insertion loss is around 1.6dB. The measured result has a reasonably good agreement with the simulated result in X-band frequency.

articleTitle: Unitary matrix pencil method for sparse linear array pattern synthesis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient approach, named unitary matrix pencil method, is presented for pattern synthesis of sparse linear arrays. An equivalent real-valued matrix pencil can be achieved to determine the relation between element positions and new generalized eigenvalues through using the unitary transformation for the Hankel matrix with the sampled pattern data. The proposed method increases up the matching accuracy and reduces the computation complexity compared with the former matrix pencil method. Numerical examples demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Ultrathin multiband microwave absorber based on electric-field-coupled-LC resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, flexible electric-field-coupled-LC (ELC) resonator for ultrathin microwave absorbing is designed. The microwave absorber consists of three layers: periodic-arrangement ELC resonators, 1.1mm FR-4 substrate and background metallic plane. Single-band, dual-band and triple-band absorber are achieved by scaling the ELC resonators in frequency range of 5-20 GHz. Current distribution, excellent absorption rates and electric field presented in paper verify good performance of proposed absorber.

articleTitle: Suppressing characteristics of TVS device under electromagnetic pulse
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Transient voltage suppressor (TVS) device is the chief way by which the susceptibility to Electromagnetic pulse (EMP) of equipment can be decrease. Prior to each application, the TVS device has to be tested in order to evaluate its performances. In this paper, a new EMP protection performance testing system is designed and the Suppressing characteristics of four kinds of TVS device during EMP stressing, e.g., response time and clamping voltage are analyzed. It is concluded that, the clamping voltage is increasing with the augment of the injected pulse voltage; the response time is independent of the injected pulse voltage and the injected pulse width. These important conclusions are significant in improving the revolution of structure and technology of TVS device.

articleTitle: Compact SIW 3×3 butler matrix for 5G mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a compact SIW (substrate integrated waveguide) 3×3 Butler matrix (BM) for 5G mobile applications. The detailed structuring procedures, parameter determinations of each involved component are provided. To validate the 3×3 BM, a slot array is designed. The cascading simulations and prototype measurements are also carried out. The overall performance and dimension show that it can be used for 5G mobile devices. The measured S-parameters agree well with the simulated ones. The measured gains are in the range of 8.1 dBi ~ 11.1 dBi, 7.1 dBi ~ 9.8 dBi and 8.9 dBi ~ 11 dBi for port 1~3 excitations.

articleTitle: High speed motion compensation for terahertz ISAR imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Due to great advantages in anti-stealth and wide bandwidth, the Terahertz Inverse synthetic aperture radar (THz-ISAR) imaging technique has attracted much attention in recent years. However, high resolution will intensify the dispersion effect especially for high-speed moving targets. This paper presents a new method of high speed motion compensation for THz-ISAR imaging. The proposed entropy-based method is capable of auto focusing the image in several iterations, which avoids using the time-frequency distribution. Its superiority is compared in simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Small square-shaped slot antenna for wearable passive UHF RFID tags
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a slot antenna with the footprint size of 4 × 4 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.12λ × 0.12λ at 915 MHz) for wearable passive UHF RFID tags. In addition to the main radiating slot, cuts made into the surrounding conductor increase the antenna radiation efficiency and help to self-match the antenna impedance with the RFID microchip in the body-worn configuration. Antenna structure is uniplanar and optimised for a low-permittivity textile substrate. The measured attainable read range of the tag is 2.5 metres when affixed to the upper back of a test subject.

articleTitle: Advanced microfabrication techniques for the development of millimeter-wave wafer-level waveguide devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This work presents an overview of advanced microfabrication techniques for the fabrication of millimeter-wave waveguide devices on the wafer-level. Using thick sacrificial photoresists to form the waveguide channel, a new class of millimeter-wave waveguide devices is discussed, which already show very promising results. These devices offer the benefits of full integration of millimeter-wave components with IC design, and lay the foundation for a new class of monolithic millimeter-wave RF front end components and systems.

articleTitle: Scattering by 2D continuous periodic structure modeled with the electric field integral equation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper describe a surface integral equation(SIE) method for efficient computation of electromagnetic fields scattered from 2D continuous periodic structure. The proposed method calculated with the electric field integral equation (EFIE) and relies on the evaluation of the periodic Green's functions performed with Ewald's method. The boundary edge is processed to ensure continuity. Numerical results validate the accuracy of the improved method in detail.

articleTitle: A novel miniaturization Quasi Yagi-Uda antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel miniaturezation Quasi Yagi-Uda antenna based capacitive loading technique and new layout. In the proposed antenna, the horizontal size of the proposed antenna is reduced by adding vertical metallic strips at the end of the driver and reflector. Meanwhile, the 1/4 wavelength transformer and balun are placed horizontally to reduce the vertical size. In this way, the overall dimensions of the proposed antenna could be decrease without much loss in other performance indicators. Then the parameters of the antenna is optimized by the software HFSS. The measurement results exhibit that the proposed antenna has a good VSWR from 902MHz to 928MHz and its gain is about 5.8dBi at 915MHz. And the overall size of proposed antenna is 110mm*105mm that is around λ/3 × λ/3 where λ is the wavelength of the centre frequency.

articleTitle: Diagnose element failures of phased antenna arrays with a single fixed receiving probe
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An element failure diagnosis method for phased array antenna is proposed. The method is based on the matrix method by solving inverse matrix to retrieve the excitations of the antenna under test. Taking advantages of the phase shift of the excitation, the receiving probe can be fixed during the measurement process to reduce positioning errors. The results have good accuracy to identify the locations of failure elements.

articleTitle: Microstrip reflectarray for generation of vortex electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: One type of orbital angular momentum (OAM) reflectarray antenna is proposed to radiate the vortex electromagnetic wave. The phase distribution of far-zone field for the 1st mode and the 2nd mode OAM, simulated by FEKO software, demonstrates the phase singularity and vortex.

articleTitle: Design of compact bandpass filter based on EMSIW cavities
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a compact bandpass filter based on stacked eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide (EMSIW) resonators. By properly constructing the feeding and coupling topology of four EMSIW cavities, the proposed filter not only exhibits compact size, but also achieves enhanced selectivity by virtue of its three transmission zeros (TZs). A novel cross-coupled structure which contributes to TZs is constructed without increasing the circuit size compared with the conventional fourth-order cross-coupled model. The filter is designed and fabricated on two lays of substrate, good agreement between simulated and measured results is also obtained.

articleTitle: A compact dual-band patch antenna using metamaterial structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a single-layered dual-band patch antenna using a CRLH mushroom-like metamaterial structure. The antenna is compact, it can achieve maximum gains of 2.29 dBi at 2.76 GHz and 7.06 dBi at 4.27 GHz, with a monopole-like and a patch-like radiation pattern, respectively. The bandwidths for the reflection coefficient less than -10 dB are 28 MHz at the low frequency band and 130 MHz at the high one. The proposed compact dual-band antenna exhibits an overall size of 0.18λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ×0.18λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ×0.03λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, at 2.76 GHz.

articleTitle: Analiysis of typical ground clutter statistical characteristics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to obtain more understanding about the regularity of ground clutter distribution, two types of measuring data about grass and soil have been taken in the Object Spectrum Characteristic Laboratory. This paper provided an analysis of the amplitude statistics of these data using Lognormal, Weibull, Gamma, Exponential and Rayleigh distribution. Their goodness-of-fit carried out by Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test after the estimation of the distribution parameters. The results show that with the grazing angle increased, scattering coefficient also increased, but hold the line varied from frequency. The scattering coefficient of grass and soil obey Weibull distribution in different grazing angles, and they cannot be distinguished by the distribution characteristics.

articleTitle: Bandwidth enhanced compact dual-band smart watch antenna for WLAN 2.4/5.2 GHz application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a bandwidth enhanced compact dualband antenna for smart watch is proposed. By using the T-shaped feeding structure on the top of FR-4 substrate, dual-band characteristics are achieved in WLAN (2.4/5.2 GHz) bands. To enhance the bandwidths in WLAN (2.4/5.2 GHz) bands, two parasitic elements on the top of FR-4 substrate and a rectangular slot on the bottom of FR-4 substrate are utilized in this antenna. In addition, to apply the proposed antenna to a practical smart watch, a cubic phantom is used to analyze the antenna performance.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband metasurface for radar cross section reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An ultra-wideband metasurface is designed for suppressing the specular electromagnetic wave reflection or backward radar cross section (RCS). Square ring structure is chosen as the basic meta-atoms. A new physical mechanism based on size adjustment of the basic meta-atoms is proposed for ultrawideband manipulation of electromagnetic (EM) waves. Based on hybrid array pattern synthesis (APS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, the selection and distribution of the basic meta-atoms are optimized simultaneously to obtain the ultra-wideband diffusion scattering patterns. The metasurface can achieve an excellent RCS reduction in an ultra-wide frequency range under normal incidence. The new proposed mechanism greatly extends the bandwidth of RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband reflectarray with multi-resonance elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel single-layer four square-loop reflectarray element with linear polarization is investigated in this paper. The proposed element shows a large phase variation and a smooth phase-frequency curve. Multi-frequency matching method is applied to achieve wideband performance. A center-fed 24×20 microstrip reflectarray operating from 8 to 18 GHz has been designed and simulated. It has a focus-to-diameter ratio (F/D) of 1.2 and is fed by a wideband Vivaldi antenna.

articleTitle: Extracting maximum efficiency of wireless power transfer in endoscopic capsule applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a maximum efficiency extracting technique is presented for endoscopic capsule's Wireless Power Transfer (WPT). Instead of conventional regulators, a DC-DC Bulk LTC3129-1 with Maximum Power Point Control (MPPC) capability is adopted to boost the power conversion efficiency of the WPT receiver (including RF-DC rectifier and DC-DC Converter) up to 60%. Measurements validate that DC-DC Bulk LTC3129-1 outperforms the LDO over the operational power ranges from 22.5dBm to 25dBm. The presented WPT receiver system with DC-DC Bulk is practical for the maximum efficiency extraction of WPT in endoscopic capsule applications.

articleTitle: Parametric analysis of vertical incidence reflectivity of conformal PML
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The vertical incidence reflectivity of conformai perfectly matched layer (PML) is an essential property that can demonstrate partly the error and efficiency of absorbing boundary condition (ABC). To design the high-performance conformal PML, some parametric analysis of vertical incidence reflectivity is implemented in this paper. By deducing and solving the recursion relation of reflection coefficient of multilayer conformal PML, the influence trends of basic parameters on the reflection coefficient of multilayer spherical PML are obtained. It is proved that this parametric analysis approach is reliable and valuable for creating the ideal conformal PML.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the nonlinear response of receiver mixer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper founds a response model of the mixer. Three kinds of nonlinear elements are included in this model. The three nonlinear elements are negative gain element, switch element, and port coupling. This model is accurate to compute the response of the mixer. Adopting this model, this paper simulates the response of mixer, and draws the conclusion.

articleTitle: Investigation of the roles of filters for a harmonic FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the importance of RF bandpass filters in a harmonic FMCW radar system is investigated. The harmonic radar system is designed using the National Instruments (NI) AWR Design Environment, and simulation is performed with the Visual System Simulator (VSS). The roles of band-pass filters are analyzed. System level simulation indicates that to detect the weak harmonic signal from a non-linear target, a band-pass filter on the transmitter path is necessary to block the harmonics of the carrier signal, a band-pass filter on the local oscillator path is important to block the fundamental frequency leakage, and another band-pass filter before the LNA on the receiver chain is indispensable to reject the fundamental frequency captured by the receive antenna. Moreover, the group delays of the filters need to be properly controlled for reliable range detection.

articleTitle: Near-field scattering characteristic of complex targets in local illumination scenario
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to compute the near-field scattering characteristic of complex targets in local illumination scenario. The scattering characteristic of one typical fuze target is computed by using Near-Field MLFMA which match well with the measurement results, verifying the veracity of the algorithm in the model of this paper.

articleTitle: A novel on-orbit calibration technique for large phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Large APAA (active phased array antenna) contains hundreds of elements and the performance of an APAA will degrade over time as a result of changes mainly in the solid-state components. For airborne and satellite-borne APAA applications, ground-based calibration sources may be difficult or impractical to implement due to the constraints of volume and resources. In this paper, a novel self-calibration technique is proposed in order to measure the amplitude and phase degradation of each active array element. By fast and accurate measurement with little satellite resource cost, this technique can be easily applied to the on-orbit diagnostics and self-calibration for APAA. The technique presented in this paper takes the advantages of APAA properties that the attenuator and phase-shifter in each element module can be controlled flexibly while operating on-orbit measurements. The dedicated internal passive calibration elements are employed in array aperture to measure the complex electric fields between each other active array elements. During the process of measurement, one active element needs to be rotated in three phase intervals, while other non-rotating active elements set to the maximum attenuation. Then this process is repeated for every active element to work out the phase and amplitude distribution of array aperture. The calculation results shown in this paper match the requirements of amplitude and phase measurement accuracy for an on-orbit phased array self-calibration.

articleTitle: Power adaption for half-duplex relay-based D2D communication underlaying cellular network
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The existing half-duplex relay-based device-to-device (D2D) communication equips with single antenna infrastructure and receives and transmits signals in two equivalent slots which lead to poor performance in term of rate achievement. To solve this problem, we propose a new relay-based D2D scheme with two-antenna infrastructure and bring in slot splitting factor to divide one frame into double unequal slots. The simulation results show that the proposed relay-based D2D communication scheme outperforms the existing half-duplex and full-duplex relay-based D2D communication in term of achievable rate.

articleTitle: Antenna array pattern correction with failure elements using AGA
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A approach using the adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) is proposed for array failure correction in digital beam forming of arbitrary arrays. In this article we use adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) change the excitation of elements to improve the performance of array with failed elements. Numerical examples are presented to show the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Dielectric characterization of Guo Biao concrete
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents an application of noninvasive near-field technique for wireless structural health monitoring. The dielectric constants of Guo Biao concrete specimens were studied by means of regression modelling. The aim is to obtain the nominal values of dielectric constant of Guo Biao concrete.

articleTitle: A CPW-fed dual-band high gain antenna using metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band high gain antenna with metasurface (MS) is designed and analyzed. This proposed antenna consists of two same substrates which are fixed by four plastic screws. The dual-band antenna on the top substrate is fed by the coplanar waveguide (CPW), whereas the planar MS consisting of uniform metallic patch cells is fabricated on the second substrate. The extended branch of antenna is used to achieve the dual-band performance, thereby increasing the operating bandwidth. Furthermore, the MS works as a high-efficient radiator, which helps to enhance the relative radiation gain. After optimization, the antenna is capable of having impedance bandwidths of about 22.44% (11.71%), maximum gains of about 8.74 dB (9.53 dB) at 4 GHz (5.8 GHz), and 3.03 dB as well as 3.56 dB relative radiation gains at two resonant points respectively. The measured results agree well with the anticipation.

articleTitle: Design and experimental verification of a Fast Reduced-Dimension SAGE algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for multipath component (MPC) parameters requires high computational complexity, resulting in low efficiency in channel measurement campaigns. In this paper, a new method, called Fast Reduced-Dimension SAGE (FRDS) algorithm, is proposed to estimate the parameters such as excess delay, power, and angle-of-arrival/departure (AoA/AoD). By sounding channels using pseudo-noise sequences in the time domain, FRDS utilizes the extracted correlation function of the received array signals to perform iterative ML calculation, instead of using baseband signal samples. Thus the data set size and computational complexity are reduced significantly. A channel sounder has been developed and the FRDS algorithm is validated by field experiments. It is shown that FRDS can effectively improve the efficiency of channel measurement and modeling.

articleTitle: Isosceles right triangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The expressions of the transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes of the isosceles right triangular waveguides with unusual boundary conditions are discussed in this paper. Based on the initial solution formed using a finite sum of rectangular harmonics, boundary conditions are discussed, and TE and TM mode expressions are presented in this paper for the isosceles right triangular waveguides with all the possible boundary conditions. Transverse modal field distributions are given for the different isosceles right triangular waveguides.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of pulse Doppler radar system based on SystemVue code
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Pulse Doppler radar is a kind of the pulse radar which is based on Doppler effect and it has an excellent ability of anti-interference that it can detect moving target from strong noise. In this paper, we will study the modeling and simulation of pulse Doppler radar based on SystemVue code that is an electronic system level simulation tool, and the key techniques include speed of ambiguity resolution algorithm, Pulse-Doppler processing, and constant false alarm detection. The functionality and features of pulse Doppler radar are verified and SystemVue shows its superiority on electronic system design.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival estimation using sum co-array of coprime arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, direction of arrival (DOA) estimation using sum co-array of coprime arrays is studied. The array geometry can be represented as the kronecker product of those of two coprime arrays. This array structure can reduce the aperture loss when extracting the subarrays, which are jointly used to achieve high resolution and unique DOA estimation via low computational propagator method. Compare to original coprime arrays based method, the proposed algorithm achieves better estimation results. Besides, the proposed method has low complexity for it requires neither peak search nor eigenvalue-decomposition. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Internal network boundary condition incorporated in FDTD to efficiently modeling low-profile periodic structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Internal network boundary condition (INBC) incorporated in Finite-difference Time-domain (FDTD) algorithm to efficiently simulate low-profile periodic structure is proposed. The method is based on vector fitting (VF) approach to approximate the 2-port Y-matrix network parameters of the periodic structure by a series of partial fractions in terms of real or complex conjugate pole-residue pairs, which generates an internal network boundary condition including the frequency-dependent self- and mutual admittance characteristics of the periodic structure. A discrete-time equation of INBC is then derived and incorporated in FDTD update equations by Laplace transform and time central difference methods. For demonstration, one frequency selective surface (FSS) structure is analyzed, which indicates the validity of accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A modified multiple self-adaptive thresholds fast feature points extraction algorithm based on image gray clustering
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Traditional FAST feature points extraction algorithm are widely used in object detection, target tracking and image matching. Generally, the detection threshold of FAST algorithm is a constant which is determined artificially before the experiment. It can't satisfy the extract requirement of different image feature points. Moreover, a single threshold does not suitable for images with large changes in gray scale range. This paper proposed an improved threshold algorithm based on gray clustering which is defined multiple self-adaptive thresholds algorithm. Firstly, K-means clustering algorithm is used in gray image. According to the difference of gray level, images are divided into 3 categories. Secondly, each category calculates the adaptive threshold respectively. Finally, according to the different thresholds, the image feature points can be extracted by traditional FAST algorithm. The algorithm used multiple adaptive detection thresholds to avoid constant threshold disadvantages in traditional FAST algorithm detection. The simulation results showed that the proposed algorithm can adapt to different illumination conditions, and the duplication of the feature points is improved by 30%, compared with the traditional FAST algorithm.

articleTitle: Broadband circularly polarized antenna with high gain for Ku-band applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel broadband circularly-polarized (CP) antenna fed by strip-line is proposed. The CP operation is achieved by corners truncated and can be significantly improved by introducing a pair of half loop strips around two opposite corners of the square patch. The bandwidths for the axial ratio (AR <; 3 dB) and relative impedance (|S11| <; -10 dB) is 7.6% (16-17.2 GHz). The proposed antenna also has a peak gain of about 6.8 dBi@16.5 GHz and has a stable radiation pattern over the entire CP frequency band.

articleTitle: Measurement and suppression of electromagnetic interference to speed sensor of CRH380BL electric multiple unit
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The speed sensor of CRH380BL electric multiple unit (EMU) would be affected by the electromagnetic interference (EMI) caused by pantograph-catenary arc when pantograph dropped, which could result in the abnormal locking of car door. A method to absorb the energy of high frequency by nesting magnetic ring on the cable shield of speed sensor was proposed and tested to achieve the purpose of suppressing radiation interference.

articleTitle: Modeling of low noise amplifier based on volterra series with recursive least square algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The low noise amplifier (LNA) is a significant device in RF front-end. In this paper, a straight and efficient modeling method for LNA based on the Volterra series with recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm is proposed. Instead of calculating the high nonlinearity order of Volterra kernels, the proposed method extracts the first three order Volterra kernels characterizing the memory effect to construct a model of LNA, which is measured and simulated by the proposed method, and a good agreement is confirmed.

articleTitle: Blind separation of human motions based on independent component analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, a single-input multiple-output (SIMO) continuous-wave Doppler radar sensor (DRS) system is designed and implemented for motion separation. A blind motion separation approach is proposed to separate the combinations of triangular and sinusoidal motions can with amplitude accuracy. Experiments show that combinations of different motions can be linearly separated. These results imply the potential in practical applications of human motion detection and separation.

articleTitle: Unitary matrix pencil method for multi-beam sparse linear array pattern synthesis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we present a method for the synthesis of multiple beams sparse array pattern based on the unitary matrix method (UMP). A Hankel block matrix is constructed from the sample data of the multiple beams pattern, we can obtain the corresponding excitation for each beam and the sparse array element position through the generalized value decomposition of the equivalent matrix pencil. The numerical example is conducted to validate the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A single-feed dual-band circularly polarized microstrip antenna with spiral slots
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact, low-cost, dual-band circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna with single-feed operating at both 1555 MHz and 2500 MHz bands is designed in this paper. The circular patch of the antenna is slotted with four complementary spiral grooves for dual-band radiation. The bandwidths of |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10dB of the antenna are 42 MHz centered at 1555 MHz and 25 MHz centered at 2500 MHz, respectively. The frequency ratio (FR) of the upper to lower operating frequencies is about 1.6. The 3dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths are 846 MHz at the lower band and 229 MHz at the upper band. Measured results agree with simulated ones, which show that right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) radiation can be achieved in these two bands.

articleTitle: A broadband CPW fractal antenna for RF energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel broadband CPW fed fractal antenna is proposed for wireless RF energy harvesting. Based on circular patch, the equilateral triangle slot is made to form a 2-iteration fractal antenna. Using FR4 with the dielectric constant of 4.4 as substrate, the antenna is simulated and fabricated. The bandwidth of the antenna is from 0.88GHz to 8.45GHz which covers 2.4GHz > 5GHz WLAN bands and mobile communication bands for 2G/3G/4G. The input impedance is 50Ω and the measured return loss is more than 10 dB in the whole bandwidth.

articleTitle: High-efficiency and wideband bridge linking waveguide waves and spoof surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons (SSPPs) have shown many significant practical applications for new waveguide and devices in microwave frequency range. For these practical applications, it requires efficient conversion between spoof surface plasmon polaritons and guided waves when feeding energies into and extracting signals from functional plasmonic waveguides or devices. In this work, a smooth bridge between the plasmonic waveguide structure and the traditional waveguide port is proposed. Two oblique wedge waveguide connectors are respectively used to compress the field energy and provide impedance conversion. A grade varied patches array is etched on the copper grounded substrate, that helps mitigating the momenta difference. Simulation results show good transmission performance under rather broad bandwidth. The proposed design scheme of the matching transition is also valid for other types of plane plasmonic waveguide.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-based low-profile broadband hexagonal-grid-slotted patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A metamaterial-based broadband low-profile hexagonal-grid-slotted patch antenna is presented. By specially slotting the radiating patch, a periodic array of series capacitor loaded metamaterial hexagonal patch cell is formed, and excited through the coupling aperture in a ground plane right underneath and parallel to the M-shaped slot at the center of patch. By exciting two adjacent resonant modes simultaneously, wideband impedance matching and consistent radiation are achieved. The proposed hexagonal-grid-slotted patch antenna with a low profile of 0.06λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the center of operating wavelength in the free space) achieves impedance bandwidth of 34% for 10-dB return loss with the gain of 9-11dBi.

articleTitle: A metallic 3D printed K-band ridged horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a metallic 3D printed K-band (18-26.5 GHz) antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a circle horn antenna, a flange and a transition from flange to horn antenna. For improved performance of the antenna at upper band, double ridges are printed symmetrically at the inside wall of the horn antenna. At the same time, two gradual ridges connect the double ridges and flange for a smoothly impedance transition.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave channel measurement and spatial characteristics for indoor environments
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, an indoor channel measurement campaign in conference room and corridor is introduced, using multi-dimension wideband channel sounder to obtain spatial channel characteristics at 25.5, 28, 37.5 and 39.5 GHz in various elevation angles. Due to proper separation of frequency, two multi-frequency path loss models considering cross polarization discrimination (XPD) factor are proposed to compare with previous inaccurate results. The redefined rms spatial angular spread calculated method avoids over estimation of azimuth angle spread and is used to evaluate elevation information with field measured results. Benefiting from two transmitter locations measured in corridor, the Tx inside the corridor performs to have less spread in delay and azimuth with better coverage. The indoor millimeter-wave (mmW) spatial channel parameters developed here lays a useful promotion to determine future licensed mmW bands and their channel models.

articleTitle: Water extraction of SAR image based on region merging algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: SAR (Synthetic aperture radar) has the advantages that it can be observed all day long and all weather. Space borne SAR is able to observe the target area periodically, therefore the extraction of lakes using SAR image is more and more widely used. The detection and update of lake plays an important role in water resources managing, water environment monitoring and watershed management. The traditional image segmentation method can hardly extract the lake quickly and accurately due to the impact of the wind, the differences of backscattering characteristic and the influence of noise on SAR images. Taking Hulun Lake as an example, this paper presents a combination of coarse and fine based region merging algorithm for SAR image to extract lakes automatically. The results show that the improved algorithm increases the accuracy of lake surface extraction and reduces the time complexity of region merging.

articleTitle: Progress on microwave devices fabricated using stereolithography 3-D printing technique
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, recent advances in metallic coated photosensitive-resin-based microwave passive devices fabricated using stereolithography 3-D printing technique are reviewed. Considerations in the design and fabrication technology of these devices are discussed. This new family of 3-D printed microwave devices have advantages of light weight and flexibility in structural design over the conventional ones made from metals.

articleTitle: Rotating-element electric-field vector(REV) calibration method based on power measurement for phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The REV method based on power measurement can avoid the phase measurement, so the calibration can reach a high stability especially in high frequency. A modified method that can significantly reduce the phase-shifting error in REV method is presented in this paper. It is verified that increasing the bits of phase shifter and measuring states can reduce the effect of such error and improve the calibration accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband filtering power divider with stub-loaded ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband filtering power divider is designed by employing a stub-loaded ring resonator. The first two resonant modes of the ring resonator are excited to form the filtering passband. To improve the passband skirt, two transmission zeros near the passband are then introduced by mounting an open stub along the ring resonator. After installing two coupled lines at two output ports, one additional transmission pole could be generated and a good in-band response is achieved. Finally, a prototype of the proposed power divider is designed and fabricated. The measured 14-dB fractional bandwidth is about 60 % and the in-band isolation achieved 20 dB from 1.05 GHz to 1.87 GHz.

articleTitle: Recent advances on the high frequency electromagnetic modeling and simulation techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, the scattering field excited by the perfect conducting quadratic surface is comprehensively studied. The numerical steepest descent path method (NSDP) is invoked to calculate the high oscillatory physical optics integral. Its result agrees very well with the Gordon's integral than asymptotical method. Moreover, the computation effort for the highly oscillatory integral is frequency independent. In the end, we use the Fourier quadrature method to calculate transition and deep shadow scattering field excited by the conducting cylinder.

articleTitle: Design of FSS-based UWB absorber using multi-layer modified circular ring
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-layer modified circular ring absorber is introduced on the basis of the ordinary circular ring. Simulations results are shown that the absorptivity is more than 90% in the frequency range from 5.5GHz to 19GHz under the normal incidence, the bandwidth is achieved up 13.5GHz, covering C, X, and Ku bands. The FSS structure exhibits the stable response for both TE and TM polarizations. The detailed results of different incident wave angles (0° /15° /30° /45°) are also given in this paper.

articleTitle: A beamwidth modified model for calculation of reflected level of quiet zone in anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In calculation of reflected level of quiet zone in anechoic chamber, a spot emission model is often used to simulate antennas' characteristic. The model is useful in low frequency and not in microwave frequency because microwave antennas are of sharper directivity. In this paper, a new emission model, which can be used in microwave frequency, has been derived from Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction formulation. It has been demonstrated that new model is more appropriate to actualities than spot model.

articleTitle: A new shooting and bouncing rays algorithm based on unigraphics and its application in cavity targets
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Method of Shooting Bouncing Rays (SBR) can quickly calculate radar cross section (RCS) of cavity targets and handle multiple scattering between target structures as a high-frequency algorithm. In this paper, a novel method of ray tracing has been proposed by utilizing Unigraphics (UG) 3D modeling features and secondary development tool UG open application program interface (UG/OPEN API). Compared with the traditional ray tracing method, SBR based on UG can make tube and real model surface intersect, having high computing speed and accurate ray tracking, and it can calculate RCS of the cavity targets accurately.

articleTitle: Low profile dual-polarized circular patch antenna with HIS reflector for TT&C system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A coax-feed low profile dual-polarized circular patch antenna with high impedance surface (HIS) reflector is presented. The proposed antenna contains two pairs of H-shaped slots on the two bow-tie shaped patches separately, which keep the cross polarization under −39 dB. By introducing two short pins, the isolation between the two ports remains more than 40 dB in the whole bandwidth. Low profile and high front-back ratio characteristics are achieved by using the HIS reflector. The height of the antenna is less than λ/8 and the front-back ratio is better than 30 dB. The proposed antenna which covers a −10-dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of 2.28–2.75 GHz can be used for S-band telemetry track and command (TT&C) system.

articleTitle: Novel coil design for wideband wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Wireless power transfer has been widely used in various applications and been intensively researched recently, especially after the mid-range resonant inductive coupling was proposed. Most resonant inductive coupling systems are narrowband, which limits their adaptability and application. A spherical helix is proposed for a wireless power transfer system with a wider bandwidth. The system with the proposed design shows high efficient power transfer within a wide band.

articleTitle: Efficient microwave rectifier over wide input power range for wireless energy transfer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel rectifier topology in an attempt to extend its operating input power range. With the addition of n-channel Field Effect Transistor (n-FET) that acts as an adaptive switch, the rectifier is able to adjust automatically between low and high input power modes and remains efficient over a wide input power range. A 1-GHz prototype is designed and the measurement shows that the efficiency level stays above 50% from -4 dBm to 20 dBm, and achieves peak efficiency of 81% at 17 dBm of input power.

articleTitle: Analysis of conductor losses of planar transmission lines with surface roughness by the method of lines
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Accurate modeling of planar transmission line is very important in microwave communication and radar systems, especially at high frequencies. The present paper computes the conductor loss of planar transmission line in full-wave band by the method of lines considering the surface roughness. The new concept presented here derives a complex surface impedance from conductivity Gradient Model, reflecting the effects of surface roughness, which can easily be incorporated as boundary condition into the method of lines. The computer storage is reduced effectively with ensuring simulation accuracy. The proposed method can be applicable in modeling of complex planar microwave circuits.

articleTitle: Design of reflective surface for cross-polarization conversion and RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents the design of novel surface that can convert the incident EM-waves into its cross-polarized (orthogonal) component at millimeter wave frequencies. The unit cell composing the surface has a cut of wire along the diagonal with two closed rings above and below. The unit cell has three resonance frequencies at 84.32GHz, 85.6GHz, and 87.38GHz at which the polarization conversion reaches 100%. The results show a strong cross-polarization conversion from about 84.2GHz to 87.9GHz with polarization conversion efficiency of more than 83%. Moreover, if the surface is designed using the proposed unit cell and its mirrored one, the reflected EM-wave can be controlled freely and Monostatic RCS reduction can be achieved with diffuse reflection like backscattered RCS field pattern.

articleTitle: Numerical study of human head RCS and SAR at 0.9–2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This study discusses about the findings of a radar cross section (RCS) and Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) study of human head at 0.9-2.45 GHz based on full-wave numerical model simulations. The homogeneous SAM head were used to simulate the human head. We analyze the RCS and SAR of the human head as a function of aspect angle and frequency, drawing important conclusions in terms of the magnitude of the human electromagnetic signature. The result of our study can help researchers to consider the scattering and absorption of human head.

articleTitle: A semicircular metamaterial-loaded monopole filtering antenna with high selectivity and harmonics suppression
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A wideband filtering antenna with high selectivity and stopband harmonics suppression based on terminated coupled-line structures and monopole antenna is proposed in this letter. The filtering antenna possesses a flat gain response within the operational band and a good band-edge selectivity. To verify the design, a prototype operating at 3.2 GHz has been fabricated and measured. The experimental results, which are in good agreement with simulations, demonstrate that the filtering antenna exhibits excellent impedance matching, flat gain response, and high selectivity. Moreover, the design of the filtering antenna is presented and discussed in detail in this paper.

articleTitle: The implementation of precise delay in SAR echo simulation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: SAR echo simulator plays an important role in space-borne SAR development. The echo delay precision in the SAR echo simulator reflects the quality of the echo, which is limited due to the limited AD sampling rate. In this paper, a non-integer delay filter algorithm based on Lagrange interpolation is proposed to realize the precise echo delay, which uses the approximation in frequency domain. The results show that the method is effective and is put into use in the actual space-borne SAR echo simulation.

articleTitle: Detection of radiometer radio frequency interference with power-law detector
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The radiometer for remote sensing is susceptible to be interrupted by the radio frequency interference (RFI). An algorithm for pulsed-sinusoidal radiometer RFI detection based on the time-frequency domain power-law statistics is presented in this paper.
