The short time Fourier transform (STFT) is firstly employed to obtain spectrograms of radiometer signal, and the law-power detector is then computed to achieve the detection of RFI. The preliminary results show that radiometer RFI can be detected effectively and the threshold setting for the presented algorithm is easier than that of the temporal and spectral RFI detection methods.

articleTitle: Antenna array coupling reduction based on stacked EBG structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A coupling reduction method is proposed by using stacked electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure for a two-element antenna array. The stacked EBG is a periodic multilevel layered electromagnetic band gap structures (PML-EBG). The PML-EBG is set in the middle of two identical patch antennas with distance of 0.13λ. The proposed antenna operates at 2.55GHz. A good isolation is achieved by the use of the PML-EBG structures. The results shown that about 30dB isolation is achieved compared with the antenna array without the proposed decoupling structure.

articleTitle: Compact spiral antenna for dual-band on-body applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact dual-band spiral antenna is proposed for on-body applications in this paper, operating at 402 MHz Medical Device Radiocommunications Service (MedRadio) band and 2.45 GHz Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. Initially, a spiral-shaped dipole is adopted to form a miniaturized wearable antenna resonant at 402 MHz to communicate with implanted devices. In addition, four rectangular patches are attached in bottom layer to improve the impedance matching at MedRadio band. Finally, a pair of rectangular strips is introduced to form an additional required resonance at ISM band.

articleTitle: Holographic imaging algorithm for millimeter wave imaging system with sparse antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the effective phase center error for sparse array sampling in active millimeter wave imaging system is analyzed and compensated. Holographic imaging algorithm for millimeter wave imaging system with sparse antenna array is developed by incorporating the phase center error compensation technique. Numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Wideband high-gain fabry-perot resonator antenna with small footprint dielectric superstrates and a conical short horn
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A wideband high-gain Fabry-Perot resonator antenna (FPRA) is proposed. It composts of a small feeding antenna, a PEC ground and three truncated dielectric slabs with small footprint that achieve positive reflection phase response. Simulations show that high-gain and wideband performance is achieved. A conical horn is then incorporated with the FPRA to further enhance its gain. Both simulations and experiments were carried out to validate the designs, and good agreements are obtained. Simulated results shows that the final antenna with a peak gain of 24.0 dBi and a 3-dB gain bandwidth of more than 33.7% (11.1GHz-15.6GHz) is developed.

articleTitle: Coherently integrated cubic function based Doppler parameters estimation for moving-target imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel moving target imaging algorithm is proposed based on coherently integrated cubic phase function (CICPF) for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system. The CICPF algorithm can solve the identifiability problem caused by cubic phase function (CPF) when dealing with multicomponent signals. Moreover, the CICPF algorithm can estimate the parameters of multicomponent signals without searching procedures and can acquire high anti-noise performance due to its coherent accumulation procedure. With estimated Doppler parameters, high-quality imaging for moving targets can be obtained. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic simulation of transmission line structures using M1-D FDTD method on mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is one of the most popular computational methods for solving electromagnetic problems. The common platforms for FDTD simulations all this while are usually the computers or workstations. Exploiting the increasing computational capacity of smart hand-held mobile devices, multiple one-dimensional (M1-D) FDTD method is developed to perform electromagnetic simulation of transmission line structures on pads or phones. Based on the M1-D FDTD method, electromagnetic waves propagation along the transmission lines can be observed in time domain while simulation is in progress. Such transient observation of wave propagation could help engineers to carry out quick initial design and analysis of transmission line structures. It could also help students to better understand the operating principles of transmission line structures through real-time visualizations. Several examples are simulated and demonstrated using M1-D FDTD method on iPad, which include a microstrip filter loaded with open or shorted stubs, a branch-line coupler and a coupled line filter, etc. These simulations show the real-time propagations of electromagnetic waves in the circuits. Their corresponding S parameter frequency responses agree well with those obtained by Advanced Design System (ADS).

articleTitle: Research on the FDTD method of scattering effects oof three dimensional dusty plasma
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this article, the JE convolution-finite-difference time-domain (JEC-FDTD) method is applied to research the influence of the electromagnetic (EM) wave's scattering characteristics on the dusty plasma. The correlation properties of dusty plasma are analyzed by using radar cross section (RCS). This study provides some insights for the dusty plasma. Meanwhile, some valuable conclusions are achieved.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable thinned arrays for satellite antennas application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper describes an approach with reconfigurable thinning array in order to reject sidelobe interference or suppress interference for satellite antennas application. With the remaining active elements Reconfiguration, the thinned array can decrease the peak sidelobe level or place a null in the direction of interference.

articleTitle: A research on moving target's scattering characteristics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to research the scattering characteristics of moving targets, a simulation method applied with quasi-static theory is proposed. Firstly, the CAD model of target is established and then the all-space static RCS database for this target is set up by electromagnetics software. Secondly, the flight track is established so that the real-time posture change can be described. The attitude angles calculated from the track are the key link between static RCS and dynamic RCS. Finally, the RCS data for moving targets can be extracted by the bridge of attitude angles. The research in this paper is useful for improving the radar performance especially in the prediction in engineering application.

articleTitle: A load-independent magnetically resonant wireless power transfer system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A constant voltage output independent of loads is desirable in magnetically resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. Most of the magnetically resonant WPT systems developed so far do not have such a property. In this paper, we introduce compensation networks to the WPT systems and develop the conditions and parameters that allow the magnetically resonant coupling WPT systems to be of load independent.

articleTitle: A minimized quarter-wavelength patch antenna used for monitoring mechanical deformation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized quarter-wavelength rectangular patch antenna with coaxial feed is proposed. The resonance frequency of the proposed antenna is simulated and measured so that the relationship between its mechanical deformation and resonance frequency can be determined. Also, additional tensile tests are employed to further clarify the relationship by increasing strain increments per loading step. The simulated and measured results indicate that there is a good linear relationship between the resonance frequency shift and applied mechanical deformation, which has been used for monitoring the mechanical deformation of a structure.

articleTitle: Multi-radar data fusion imaging based on iterative adaptive algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The range resolution of the traditional single radar imaging system is limited by the bandwidth of the transmitted signal, resulting in poor image quality. This paper presents a multi-radar data fusion imaging method based on iterative adaptive algorithm (IAA). Based on the radar echo sparse representation model, this method uses the echo data of different radars to minimize the target cost function under the weighted least squares criterion. Then, we can obtain the sparse parameters and get echo data of the unknown band by interpolation and extrapolation. Finally, we realize the fusion process by getting of the radar echo of the full band. The simulation results show that the image quality is improved by the resolution of the broadband echo after fusion, which is better than that of the single sub-band, verifying the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiment of a full-range non-foster response
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We investigate the wideband response of a non-Foster element based on a radio frequency operational amplifier. Our results indicate that the input impedance of a non-Foster element co-existing with a stabilization network exhibit an inverted Lorentzian resonance. This makes its full-range frequency response satisfy the Kramers-Kronig relations. In this case, while the conventional non-Foster response can be observed in the low-frequency region on the left side of the resonance, a high-frequency non-Foster response can also be observed on the right side of the resonance. This special response can be potentially used to overcome the technical challenge in achieving radio frequency non-Foster elements.

articleTitle: A novel design of microstrip decoupling network for two-element antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a systematic design of microstrip decoupling network to reduce the mutual coupling effect between a two-element antenna array. This design is based on the eigen-mode analysis method. The achieved microstrip decoupling network is simple and easy to fabricate. A reduction of more than 20 dB in mutual coupling is obtained for a two-element monopole array with element spacing of 0.1λ by using the proposed method.

articleTitle: An UWB antenna loaded with BST for band notch
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a novel technique to design a band-notched UWB antenna by using Barium Strontium Titante (BST) is proposed. A printed slot UWB antenna with size of 16 mm× 27 mm is adopted as a basic antenna. A piece of cylindrical BST slab with 1 mm height and 2.4 mm diameter is attached on the feeding layer of the antenna to achieve band-notched characteristics. The simulated −10 dB bandwidth of the antenna without BST slab is 3.1–11 GHz. With loading of different size of BST slabs at different positions, band notches of WLAN 5 GHz (5.15–5.825 GHz) and X-band satellite communication services (7.25–7.75 GHz) are obtained respectively. The tuning of notch band is also developed by adjusting the relative permittivity of BST.

articleTitle: Fabrication and evaluation of 3D-printed heat and photonic cured graphene RFID tags on veneer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We study 3D printing of graphene UHF RFID antennas on a thin wood veneer substrate, subsequently cured by heat in an oven or photonically by pulsed Xenon flash. We present the read range results of the tags and test the effects of moisture on the tag performance. Initially the peak read ranges of both types of tags are about 4.5 meters. The read range decreases about 50 cm when the tag antenna and wood substrate absorb moisture. However, after drying, the performance of the tag returns to normal.

articleTitle: Microstrip channel behavioral model for integrated circuits and electronic systems design
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Present and future link (SerDes) design requires a strong and effective coupling between high-speed circuit design, optimization, and digital communications, its problems are different that new solutions are required. This paper proposed an analytical wireline channel model for path loss prediction for effective electronic circuits and systems design. Proposed model closely match experimental data and electromagnetic full-wave simulation data. This model is recommended for electronic circuits and systems engineers, for adequate and faster interfaces (SerDes-Serializer/Deserializer) or high-speed links designs.

articleTitle: Planar balanced-to-unbalanced power divider
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel wideband balanced-to-unbalanced filtering power dividers based on coupled lines is proposed in this paper. The multi-functional power dividers can replace various cascaded single devices to decrease integration mismatching loss and circuit size. The wideband response can be easily realized by using the coupled lines structures. In addition, a resistor is introduced in the middle of two single-ended ports to realize isolation between output ports. To verify the proposed strategy, a wideband balanced-to-unbalanced filtering power divider operating at 2 GHz is designed and fabricated with 4-dB differential-mode bandwidth of 80.5%.

articleTitle: Low-profile wideband slot-loaded dipole for base station antenna element
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A low-profile wideband unidirectional dipole antenna with U and L-shaped slots loaded is proposed. A prototype with a thickness of 0.175λ was fabricated and measured. The proposed antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 57% (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>≤ -10 dB) from the frequency of 1.56 to 2.79 GHz. The cross polarization is less than -21 dB over the operating bandwidth. The antenna has an average gain of 8.6 dBi over the frequency range 1.7-2.7 GHz.

articleTitle: A novel Doppler centroid estimation method for multi-channel HRWS SAR
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In multi-channel high-resolution and wide-swath SAR signal processing, Doppler centroid (DC) is essential for channel phase bias estimation and SAR focusing. By exploiting that an inaccurate Doppler centroid would introduce linear errors in phase bias estimation and consequently deteriorate the reconstructed Doppler spectrum, the Doppler centroid can be accurately estimated by Doppler spectrum optimisation. Experimental results based on airborne real data confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable proximity coupled antenna with frequency and polarization switching capabilities
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact reconfigurable proximity coupled antenna with frequency and polarization switching capabilities is presented in this paper. The frequency and polarization switching capabilities are realized by using six PIN diodes across an star-shaped slot on the ground plane. The proposed antenna has six different operation status including linear polarization (LP), right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) wave. Due to the frequency and polarization switching capabilities, the overall capacity of the antenna in the wireless transmissions could be potentially enlarged.

articleTitle: Approximate calculation of the horizontal electric field at ground level from inclined lightning channel in frequency-domain
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An approximate method to calculate the horizontal electric field at ground level from inclined lightning channel in frequency-domain is proposed based on the extension of Cooray formula. The validation results show that the deviation of the extended formula is closely related to the observation distance and the ground conductivity. The bigger the observation distance or the ground conductivity is, the smaller the deviation is. Moreover, the inclined angle of lightning channel and the azimuth angle of observation point have little influence on the accuracy of the extended formula, which could nearly be ignored.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling reduction of a very compact UWB-MIMO linearly tapered slot antenna using a simple stepped slot
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A very compact ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) ground linearly tapered slot Antenna (LTSA) is presented in this paper. On a cost-effective FR4 substrate, it consists of a ground plane and two microstrip feed lines. Its overall dimension is only 22×26 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. To miniaturize, two linearly tapered slots on the ground plane, acts as the main radiator. Then it does not need extra large radiation patch. In particular, a simple embedded three-level stepped slot on the central ground, brings high isolation in the whole UWB band. In addition, two rectangular slots cut in the feed lines widen the impedance bandwidth. Simulated and measured results verify S11<;-10dB and S12<;-18dB at 3.1 GHz -12 GHz and good diversity performance. Therefore, the proposed MIMO antenna is potential for portable devices applications.

articleTitle: Accuracy and stability analysis of a 3D high-order staggered FDTD for Maxwell's equations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With the aim of increasing the numerical methods' precision regarding Maxwell's equations solving, a third order staggered FDTD method is proposed in this paper. The proposed method offers a trade-off between the accuracy and the stability, through the application of a third order staggered backward differentiation for the approximation of the temporal partial derivatives, and a fourth-order central difference approximation for the spatial derivatives approximation. The analysis of the numerical dispersion and the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition demonstrates that the proposed method is more efficient than the traditional FDTD.

articleTitle: Study of S-shaped structure in UWB antenna with dual-band notched characteristics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This article presents the application of novel S-shaped structure in peach-like UWB antenna with dual band notched characteristics. The S-shaped structure is composed by a square patch and two L-shaped slots with center symmetry. It has the advantage of small size, relatively long current path, and dual band-notched characteristics. The proposed antenna is simulated by using CST Microwave Studio to reject WLAN (5.15-5.825 GHz) and the downlink of X-band satellite communication systems (7.25-7.75 GHz) bands. Details of the S-shaped structure and antenna analysis are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: The analysis of multistep cylindrical structure on the dielectric surface for wideband radar cross section reduction at normal incidence
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper A wideband radar cross section (RCS) reduction structure applicable to rod-like targets on the dielectric surface is studied. The influence of dielectric surface lie chiefly with narrow frequency band with no more than 5dB. In addition, as for the typical frequency point at 9GHz, the discrepancy of RCS sweep of the multistep cylindrical structure near normal incidences between with and without surface is minor.

articleTitle: A novel symmetric cascaded frequency selective surface wtih butterworth response in X-band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this letter, a new technique for designing symmetric cascaded frequency selective surfaces with arbitrary bands of operation, with Butterworth band-pass responses at band of operation, is presented and experimentally verified. The technique is based on utilizing mutual admittance to represent transmission coefficient and getting a Butterworth response numerically through optimum parameter of the coupling layer. The result is a low-profile planar structure composed of two metal and three dielectric layers that acts as a spatial version of the Butterworth type microwave filter.

articleTitle: Experiment evaluation of meander mesh sheet for wireless power transmission
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper experimentally evaluates a two-dimensional wireless transmission sheet with enhanced power transmission characteristics. The sheet consists of three layers: a conducting base layer, a dielectric microwave propagation layer, and a surface layer with a conducting mesh of meander lines. The transmission characteristics at 2.45GHz evaluated by measuring show improvement of spatial uniformity and independence of coupler orientation compared to previous methods.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband circularly polarized elliptical slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper has presented the design of an elliptical slot antenna with characteristics of wide bandwidth and good circular polarization. The printed antenna consists of a microstrip line and a ground plane with an embedded elliptical slot. The wideband circular polarization is achieved by rotating the slot a proper angle around the center and adjusting the size of the slot. The obtained results can confirm that the proposed antenna has achieved a wide impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤ -10 dB) of about 75% (5-11 GHz) and the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 50% (5-10 GHz).

articleTitle: CNT-based conformal antenna design suitable for inkjet printing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We propose a theoretical study on dual-frequency conformal antenna made by carbon nanotubes (CNTs) which is suitable to be printed on commercially available paper substrate. According to the simulation result, it is found that the radius of the conformal cylindrical surface and the conductivity of CNTs contribute little to the antenna performance. By further integrated onto the textile substrate, the designed antenna is promising for wearable devices, in terms of its light-weight, low-cost, and conformal characteristics.

articleTitle: AlGaN/GaN HEMTs large signal model considering nonlinear Cds
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A high breakdown voltage AlGaN/GaN HEMTs is fabricated by using source-connected field plate (SCFP) in Dynax. The output capacitance (Cds) of this device shows a strong dependence on Vds. A modified Angelov large signal model considering Cds nonlinearity is presented to achieve a more accurate simulation on efficiency and linearity. The small signal simulation results indicate that the proposed nonlinear Cds model has a better accuracy.

articleTitle: Tone-ranging-inspired architecture for short-range radars: Theory and simulations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Short-range radars are currently gaining much attention from the RF/microwave community. In particular, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radars are usually exploited in a plurality of applications. However, to measure the absolute range of targets, they need a large transmitted bandwidth, which is an ever-crowded resource. Here, for the first time, a bandwidth-limited architecture based on the transmission of two tones closely located in the spectrum is proposed for short-range radars. Theoretical and simulation analyses confirm that this novel radar system permits unambiguous measurement of the range of multiple moving targets.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of I-shaped metamaterial with notch
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Based on the traditional I-shaped metamaterial structure, a new type of notched I-shaped structure is designed, and the reflection - transmission parameters are extracted by electromagnetic software HFSS. And the classical inversion algorithm shows that the structure can obtain the properties of permeability and dielectric constant in the range of 9.89 ~ 10.24GHz.

articleTitle: Quasi-peak — One of sensitive parameters of electromagnetic interference in communication equipment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The sensitive parameters of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) are important for the analysis of the interference mechanism and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) prediction. This paper points out that the quasi-peak may be sensitive parameter except peak and RMS, and verification tests are conducted on a VHF radio. The single frequency and amplitude modulation (AM) wave tests can tell the parameter which the equipment under test (EUT) is sensitive to, and get some necessary information of EUT. The dual-frequency tests have verified the effectiveness and rationality.

articleTitle: An efficient approach for improving the performance of airborne HF antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The working band of the airborne HF antennas is 2-30MHz (wavelength 10-150m), which can communicate over long distances. Limited by antenna size, airborne HF antennas have the disadvantages of low efficiency of radiation and impedance matching in low-band HF. This paper proposes a new method of improving the performance of HF antennas by reconfigurable antenna technology and folded monopole theory. Based on the simulation utilizing the software Ansoft HFSS and ADS, the impedance matching and efficiency of the antenna system are analyzed. The advantage on improving the performance of the new type of airborne HF antenna is verified by the comparison with that of the normal loop antennas.

articleTitle: Generalized single-source tangential equivalence principle algorithm for analysis of array structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the generalized single-source tangential equivalence principle algorithm (GSST-EPA) is proposed to solve the electromagnetic scattering of array structures with very small distance or even connected elements. This GSST-EPA can reduce the number of unknowns by half via the extinction theorem, and keep the good accuracy by using tangential field projection. Based on source reconstruction method (SRM), the new GSST-EPA can be used to solve more complex arrays. Furthermore, the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is used to accelerate the matrix-vector multiplication in the GSST-EPA. Several numerical results are given to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A low profile wide-angle scan phased array antenna with tile architecture
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A low profile wide-angle scan phased array antenna is designed in this paper. With the tile architecture, profile of the phased array antenna is reduced dramatically; in addition, the main beam of antenna array can steer to the desired direction by combining the invasive weed optimization method with the active element radiation pattern of inter-element, which includes the effects of mutual coupling. An engineering application prototype is fabricated and measured, the measured results agree well with the simulated counterpart.

articleTitle: Design of radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna using metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a radiation pattern raconfigurable antenna (RPRA) with the structure of meta-surface(MS). The antenna consists of two parts: a special MS and a slot antenna. It has good directionality, low profile and high gain. By controlling the PIN diode switches, the equivalent length of the gaps can be changed significantly. In this way, we achieve the performance of radiation pattern reconfigurable. By changing the different states of the switches, three radiation directions can be achieved. The RPRA is studied and designed to operate at 5GHz which is widely used in wireless communication system. The return loss and 3-D radiation pattern simulated by High Frequency Structure Simulator can be shown to prove the achievement of the proposal function. In addition, the working frequency of the antenna in this paper is from 4.95GHz to 5.05GHz and the peak gain can reach 9-10dB with good directionality.

articleTitle: Design of spaceborne deployable antenna and analysis of assembly tolerance
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a development of spaceborne deployable antenna array. Then a P-band dual-circular polarization flexible antenna array is designed, fabricated and measured. Moreover, the error tolerances of linear antenna array is simulated and analyzed. The proposed deployable membrane antenna array will have great potential application in spaceborne SAR system.

articleTitle: Numerical study of multiple scattering among non-spherical ice crystals at 220 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The multiple scattering (MS) effect among non-spherical ice crystals at 220GHz, a typical terahertz frequency, is numerically studied. The ice crystal ensemble with different particle sizes are generated according to the assumption of Gaussian distribution. Simulations show that MS effect can be obvious even when most of the ice crystals are small in size in comparison with the wavelength of the incident wave.

articleTitle: The calculation and analysis of shielding efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With the wide application of electronic equipment, electromagnetic radiation pollution has become the fourth-largest public nuisance after the atmospheric pollution, water pollution, noise pollution. In order to meet the requirements of electromagnetic compatibility, some shielding measures must be taken. Therefore, the study of electromagnetic shielding body's shielding effectiveness analysis and calculation has become a hot topic in the field of electromagnetic compatibility. For ventilation and heat dissipation, often need to open some holes on shielding shell, so the calculation with some small holes shield shielding effectiveness is also very necessary. This paper adopts theoretical analysis, numerical calculation and CST simulation software to calculate the shielding effectiveness of the shield.

articleTitle: Rapid estimation of near field for Cassigrain dual-reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The near field of two typical Cassegrain dual-reflector antennas which are extensively used in the aerospace field, is simulated by using the software FEKO. The electrical field strength and the equivalent near-field gain in the Fresnel region are obtained. On this basis, this paper presents a rapid estimation method of equivalent near-field gain which merely uses the far-field radiation pattern. This method can be used for rapid estimation of microwave radiation safety and analysis of electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Design and investigation of a planar microstrip-fed wideband circularly polarized antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A planar microstrip-fed wideband circularly polarized antenna has been designed and investigated in this paper. First, a wideband linearly polarized antenna consisting of a rectangular ground plane and a rectangular radiating patch has been designed. To improve the impedance matching across a wide frequency range, the feeding line is formed of a 50Ω microstrip line and a tapered impedance transformer. Furthermore, circular polarization is obtained by cutting two small rectangular patches in the radiating patch and ground plane, respectively. The modification can reach a broad axial ratio bandwidth while maintaining the wide impedance bandwidth. The obtained results show that, the antenna has an impedance bandwidth from 4.2 to 7 GHz and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth from 3.5 to 7 GHz.

articleTitle: A conformai low-profile series-fed microstrip array for aircraft applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A low-profile series-fed microstrip antenna and its 8× conformal array are presented. In this paper, the performances of the conformal array are excellent. Its obtained bandwidth is ranging from 0.94f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 1.06f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with the active voltage standing wave ratio (AVSWR) less than 2.3, where the f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is center frequency of the target band. Moreover, this proposed microstrip array can realize frequency scanning (±15°) in elevation plane and phase scanning (±30°) in azimuth plane, simultaneously. In addition, the profile is only about λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/25, which is very promising for aircraft applications. The detailed structure and simulated results of the proposed dual circularly polarized sub-array antenna will be presented.

articleTitle: An inductance loaded wideband square loop antenna with reconfigurable radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A square loop antenna (SLA) based on the hybrid high impedance surface (HHIS) substrate is investigated. For achieving reconfigurable radiation pattern, the antenna includes four feeds which can be excited both individually and simultaneously. At the four corners of the four arms, the antenna is loaded with narrow metallic strips that serve as inductances for the sake of bandwidth expanding. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth covers from 4.56 GHz to 5.96 GHz. Within the bandwidth, the SLA have a maximum gain of 11.1 dBi if only one port is excited, and it provides semi-doughnut radiation pattern with gains between 4 to 6 dBi while four ports are excited.

articleTitle: Realization of digital filter fast algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Pursuing higher speed of digital signal processing is the non-stop goal for human. When digital filter has been chosen, how to upgrade the speed of filter signal processing is a challenge for software engineer. This paper analyzes the techniques of sliding window and pipeline, and illustrates the application with two order Butterworth filter as an example. These techniques can condense the signal processing time successfully, so it's hopeful that this content can become a good reference for the signal processing engineers.

articleTitle: Impact and calibration of involving coupling device in experimental setup for differential-mode current injection method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of involving the coupling device in the radiation setup on the accuracy of the differential-mode current injection method is analyzed, when the antenna and the cable are the main coupling routes, respectively. The calibration method is then proposed correspondingly and the equivalence between the differential-mode current injection and the original radiation is achieved.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Galerkin time-domain method for devices with lumped elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A surface lumped circuit model is formulated for the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain modeling of devices with lumped elements. A leap-frog algorithm is used for time integration, resulting in an explicit and conditionally stable time-marching algorithm. A microstrip filter with four ports and two lumped elements is simulated to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: A low profile dual-band dual-polarized shared-aperture antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a shared-aperture phased array antenna with dual-band, dual-polarization and low profile is investigated. The presented antenna array operates in P-band for horizontal polarization and S-band for vertical polarization. An infinite shared-aperture array is simulated, the results shown that the array can achieve bandwidth of 35.3% and 25.8% at P- and S-band, respectively. Beam-scanning ranges of P- and Sband array are both satisfied ±20° in vertical plane and ±60° in azimuth plane with active VSWR<;2.5. The overall height of the antenna is approximately 0.17λ at the lowest frequency.

articleTitle: A new 3D MOM-GEC formulation based on reciprocity theorem: Analysis of the dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we will develop a new formulation to analyse a 3D structure. In fact, the use of the reciprocity theorem allows to extend the MOM-GEC for the resolution of 3D problems. This formulation is applied for analysing a planar antenna excited with a coaxial cable. The validation was performed by comparison with published papers and we present a good agreement.

articleTitle: Comparison of N × 2D and 3D split-step fourier methods in realistic 3D ducting conditions
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A 3D split-step Fourier method is presented and tested. It is based on a spectral representation of the discrete wave equation in cylindrical coordinates. The formulations in this method are self-consistent in the discrete domain. This method is applied to simulate the propagation with ducts retrieved after clutter data inversion. In the numerical tests, the difference between N × 2D and 3D models is not significant. Thus, in this case, considering the 3D atmosphere effects is unnecessary.

articleTitle: The application of machine learning in RCS calculation for antenna-radome system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a method based on machine learning and modified physical optics method is proposed for calculating the radar cross section (RCS) of the antenna-radome system. The scattering mechanism of the antenna-random system is estimated by the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model and the measured data in the past is analyzed. The back-propagation algorithm is chosen to train the machine learning model. In the modified physical optics method, the FSS layer is equated as an anisotropic medium, the relationship of the frequency response of the FSS layer with the incident angle, polarization and frequency is estimated by the function fitting method to improve current calculation accuracy on the radome surface. Finally the results calculated by the method proposed in this paper are validated by a real antenna-radome system.

articleTitle: 4×1 Multi-input single-output magnetic resonance beamforming wireless power transfer system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates 4×1 multi-input single-output magnetic resonance wireless power transfer system with beamforming control. The beamforming control drastically improves the transmission efficiency. The phase and amplitude of the input voltage at each TX coil are optimized to maximize the efficiency. The efficiency of the proposed system is more than 60% improvement compared with the array system without the beamforming control.

articleTitle: On the detection performance analysis of ship radar under interference environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The detection performance analysis of ship radar under interference environment are presented. The signal detection model of ship radar is constructed to analyze the detection performance. The sea clutter generation models are constructed to simulate the sea clutter's influence. And the interference models are constructed as well. Based on these models the false alarm rate and the detection threshold of ship radar under interference environment are analyzed.

articleTitle: The investigation of the electric field distribution inside the non-ideal boundary enclosure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to research the electric field distribution inside the non-ideal boundary enclosure, the calculation model of the enclosure was established based on the numerical simulation software CST, and the influence of electromagnetic wave radiation direction and polarization mode on the electromagnetic field distribution of the enclosure is analyzed. The method of testing the shielding effectiveness of the enclosure using the frequency stirring reverberation chamber is proposed. The experimental results show that the method can get the statistics electromagnetic field inside the enclosure, and the SE of the enclosure is about 8~10dB in 1~10GHz.

articleTitle: Compact UWB filter with a reconfigurable notched band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a design of compact ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter with a ultra-narrow notched band is presented. The UWB frequency responses are achieved by using a microstrip-CPW broadside coupling structure. And a pair of side-coupled short-circuited microstrip lines is introduced to generate an ultra-narrow notched band. Based on this design, by loading a pair of varactor diodes at the end of the side-coupled short-circuited microstrip lines, a reconfigurable notched-band UWB filter can also be obtained, which can avoid the existing interferences such as the RF identification (RFID) signals (6.8 GHz) and WLAN signals (5.725~5.825 GHz) in the UWB frequency range. Commercial software ANSYS HFSS is used to analyze and design this filter. Simulated results show that it has good passband/stopband performances, compact size, and notched-band reconfigurability.

articleTitle: Non-conformal IE-PE-DDM using reverse operation self-consistent evaluation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An integral equation with non-conformal and non-overlapping domain decomposition method has aroused wide interest in the engineering community. The contribution of this paper is twofold: (I) In the framework of IE-DDM, phase-extracted (PE) basis function is employed to reduce the required number of unknowns in the large and smooth sub-domain. (II) A reverse operation self-consistent evaluation (ROSE) presents a novel way to implement the Robin transmission condition, which is an attractive alternative to the traditional union mesh technique. We show that the benefit of the the application of ROSE is to redue the burden of Gaussian quadrature on the union mesh. Several numerical results will be presented to validate the efficacy and flexibility of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional through-wall imaging based on nonlinear inversion algorithms
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Through-wall imaging (TWI) is a challenging topic in the area of inverse scattering problem based microwave imaging. In this work, we experimentally investigate a TWI solution based on nonlinear inversion algorithms. Experiments are performed using a setup with the object surrounded by a closed wall. To our knowledge, this is the first experimental demonstration of TWI of objects behind a closed wall using a nonlinear inversion algorithm. These results imply the potential of TWI for practical applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of high-directivity fan-beam antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This work addresses directivity improvement of a fan-beam antenna using local constrained optimization. More specifically, it demonstrates that adjustment of elementary patch sizes of a gridded patch antenna considerably improves antenna directivity without increasing its footprint. This indicates that utilization of all available degrees of freedom, i.e., genetic algorithm (GA) optimization and continuous optimization of elementary patch dimensions and feeding position is critical to achieve the optimum performance.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic scattering properties from ocean surface in different sea areas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The bistatic specular scattering from ocean surface plays a major role in the coupling fields between super-low altitude target and ocean surface. Using the Brewster effect of ocean surface can weaken specular scattering effectively. Based on the satellite data of ocean salinity and temperature at the Western Pacific and Southeast coast, dual-Debye function is applied to build the modified model of sea water permittivity. The impacts of wind speed and frequency on electromagnetic scattering properties and Brewster effect from ocean surface in different sea areas are analyzed by using the modified two-scale model. Besides, the cut-off wavenumber at different wind speeds and frequencies is considered. The mechanism of production and changing rules of Brewster effect are summarized and analyzed.

articleTitle: Research on equivalent model of 2-D braiding reinforced composite materials based on simulation of electromagnetic shielding effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The braided reinforced composite material (BRCM) is a novel artificial electromagnetic material with wide applications in electromagnetic protection, stealth technology and electromagnetic compatibility fields, while the equivalent model of BRCM is not clear at present. The equivalent model of 2-D BRCM was established, and the shielding effectiveness (SE) of the BRCM was simulated based on electromagnetic simulation software. The spatial structure features of BRCM were analyzed, and the composite material was subdivided into multilayer anisotropic media with single yarn arrayed periodically. The electromagnetic SE prediction of 2-D BRCM was compared between the primary material and its equivalent model based on the simulation calculation. The simulation results indicate that the SE of 2-D BRCM agrees well with the SE of equivalent model. The proposed equivalent model can be used to guide the design, production and evaluation theoretically of braided reinforced electromagnetic protection materials.

articleTitle: Compact filtering crossover based on cross-shaped resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact planar filtering crossover. Such co-design circuit is equal to one conventional crossover plus two bandpass filters, which can realize circuit miniaturization. Moreover, the resonator is shared by the two transmission paths while they are isolated with each other. Thus, compactness is obtained. For validation, the filtering crossover is implemented with each path operating at 1.9 GHz. The theoretical and measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A dual operating mode antenna on flexible ground structures for wearable communications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-band dual-mode button antenna for body centric communications. Integrated on the clothes, the proposed antenna has a miniaturized flexible ground. By employing PIFA and its higher order mode, an omnidirectional pattern and a broad-side directional pattern for on-body and off-body communications are realized at lower and upper bands, respectively. With a flexible ground, this design obtains a robust reflection coefficient against the bending effect of the clothes on human body. When bending on a cylindrical phantom, the button antenna still exhibits the dual-mode characteristic. Owning to the good performance such as miniaturized dimension, dual-mode pattern and flexible ground, the proposed design is a practical candidate for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) applications.

articleTitle: A digital parallel receiver with high data rate for 16-QAM system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) is a high spectrum-utilized modulation scheme which is used extensively in digital microwave communication system. However, in QAM-based system, it is challenging to design a digital receiver with high data rate to detect signal, correct symbol-timing, and synchronize carrier effectively. In this paper, we propose a new parallel, all-digital based receiver for QAM system named HDR. This high data rate receiver is essentially a frequency-domain implementation of detection filtering and symbol-timing correction and is significantly easier to implement than the original serial receiver. Simulation results show that HDR is equivalent to both theoretical value and traditional serial receiver in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Field uniformity analysis applying Aperture-field method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With the health effects of radio fields (RF) concerned by public, many experiments exposed to RF in vivo and in vitro were studied, but some results were in the contradiction. Of all the possible reasons RF Uniformity might induce the contractions in experiments. In this paper, we proposes the Aperture-field method to evaluate field uniformity applying IEC published standard IEC 61000-40-20. The analysis software was developed to analyze the field uniformity of region of interest (ROI) with the location far from aperture antenna VS the operating frequencies applying IEC 61000-40-20, and the results is verified by SEMCAD14.8. The analysis results from the software can be used to design the biological experiments exposure to RF which should keep RF uniformity in the ROI.

articleTitle: A study of second-harmonic generation in semiconductor layer using FDTD method with hydrodynamic nonlinear Drude model
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Second-harmonic generation (SHG) has been used for demonstrating nonlinear electromagnetic responses in different materials. In this paper, the SHG in a semiconductor layer is studied under microwave and terahertz frequencies. The hydrodynamic nonlinear Drude model is implemented in the semiconductor layer to model the interactions between the carriers and the electromagnetic fields. A numerical algorithm is developed by applying the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method on both the nonlinear Drude model and the Maxwell equations. Second-harmonic component is observed in the current density of semiconductor layer and a comparison under different frequencies is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Magnetically controllable wave molding with magnetic metamaterials and metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We demonstrate a flexibly controllable molding of electromagnetic waves by designing magnetic metamaterials and metasrufaces with an array of ferrite rods under a particularly arranged bias magnetic field. The manipulation is accomplished for both the spatially propagating waves and the surface waves confined at the interface. Nonreciprocal properties associated with the magnetic surface plasmon resonance can be observed as well.

articleTitle: Fast wide-band analysis for PEC scattering problem based on characteristic basis function method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A fast wide-band algorithm that combines characteristic basis function method (CBFM) with Chebyshev approximation technique is presented to analyze PEC scattering problem over a broadband. To facilitate the analysis of electrically large targets, the CBFM is employed to substantially reduce the size of matrix equation. Further, the fast frequency sweeping can be realized by the Chebyshev approximation technique instead of solving equations at each single frequency. Numerical results show the efficiency of the approach proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the nonlinear response of receiver mixer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper founds a response model of the mixer. Three kinds of nonlinear elements are included in this model. The three nonlinear elements are negative gain element, switch element, and port coupling. This model is accurate to compute the response of the mixer. Adopting this model, this paper simulates the response of mixer, and draws the conclusion.

articleTitle: Design of thin multilayer planar absorber for active millimeter-wave imaging system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recently, a point-by-point active millimeter wave imaging system with shortened imaging time and reduced system cost and complexity is proposed. Demand for a mask to shape transceiver beam arises accordingly. Absorbing materials plays a critical role for the mask. Design of thin multilayer planar absorber in this paper. Differential evolution (DE) algorithm is implemented to solve the equivalent multi-dimensional nonlinear optimization problem. Three absorbers of less than 0.3 mm have been synthesized with at least 14 dB absorption from 0° to 30°, at 96 GHz.

articleTitle: W-band high-gain antenna arrays with low-loss gap waveguide feeding network
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, several high-gain gap waveguide (GWG) feeding antenna arrays are overviewed. Thanks to the low loss GWG feeding networks, these types of antenna arrays present wideband, high-gain and high-efficiency characteristics. They are excellent candidates for W-band applications.

articleTitle: The design of 276 GHz triple-push VCO based on 65nm CMOS process using slow-wave effect
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the design of the THz triple-push VCOs using slow-wave effect. The VCOs are implemented by 65nm CMOS process. Slow-wave coplanar waveguides(S-CPW) are applied in the VCO as inductors. Co-simulation results are given in this letter. The VCO using S-CPW consumes 49mW of DC power while generating -9.31 dBm of output power with a phase noise of -80 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from a 276 GHz carrier giving it an DC-to-RF efficiency of 0.24%.

articleTitle: Design of a terahertz circularly polarized quasi-diagonal horn antenna based on MEMS technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a terahertz(THz) circularly polarized quasi-diagonal horn antenna, which is composed of several etched silicon layers. Through adding the antipodal transition structure, we can obtain good circular polarization performance. The simulated result reveals that the bandwidth for axial ratio below 2dB from 490 GHz to 500 GHz. The return loss below -23dB from 490GHz to 500GHz. Good symmetric Gaussian beam and low cross-polarization are shown in the radiation pattern. The peak gain is higher than 23dBi from 490GHz to 500GHz. The proposed THz circularly polarized waveguide-fed horn antenna is suitable for THz imaging and communication systems.

articleTitle: Process development and failure analysis for ChipLast panel level fan-out packaging (PLP)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The demand of electronic device applications for high performance, minimization and cost effectiveness has driven the highly integrated semiconductor packaging development in recent years. Embedding die technology, which reduces package height and weight, increases the functionality and density, improves electrical and thermal performance and reduces the cost effectively, is particularly attractive in the market in recent years as well. In general, there are two main approaches for embedded die technologies including fan out wafer level package (WLP) and fan out panel level package (PLP) accordingly. Compared with fan out wafer level package, the panel solution has the advantages of using large panel processing and has maximum potential of 2.5 times cost reduction [1, 2], therefore it is very promising and attracted much attentions. While because of the panel size is much larger than wafer (12"), there are great challenges in precise alignment of die bonding to large panel, die shift during compression molding, void risks trapped in taping process, large warpage caused by the CTE (Coefficient of Thermal Expansion) between molding compound and panel, etc. As the panel size becomes larger, the process difficulty is even higher. In this paper, chip last process of panel level fan-out with 320×320mm size is developed, as shown in Figure 1. Firstly, Cu pattern circuit is fabricated by using PCB methods or substrate coreless process and bonded onto a FR4 carrier with a double side adhesive tape, and then the known good dies (KGD) are reconstructed and attached onto the substrate using pick and place machine. After the dies are encapsulated with epoxy molding compound by compression mold methods, BGA ball drop is applied onto the substrate and follow by single packages by sawing machine. The advantage of chip last is to make sure the substrate is tested with full function and dies are going to be placed onto the substrate later on so that the yield should be controlled. The challenges of this process technology, such as die jumping, die shift, delamination and warpage are presented as shown in Figure 2 and 3, and corresponding failure analysis was studied accordingly. It is found that large warpage of the substrate and voids or bubbles (without proper taping by using vacuum methods) during reflow process are the main issues and may induce delamination of the substrate and FR4 carrier, and cause die jumping and non-wetting of solders. And die shift is also found to be critical due to the limitation of die attachment precision. Therefore, reducing warpage of substrate, minimizing the trapped voids and bubbles and improving die bond accuracy are major solutions for achieving high yield and high quality of chip last processing during panel level packaging (PLP) [3,4].

articleTitle: Test method for surface charging on spacecraft dielectric materials in low-pressure environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Spacecraft surface charging effect is one of the major threats on spacecraft operational safety. In ground study, electron guns with large incident face are always adopted as simulation sources, and the surface charging test is carried out in Low-pressure environment. This paper focuses on emission stability and beam current uniformity. The results show that the electron gun should be used in conventional mode, the preheating time is 15min, the working time is 70min, and the test sample should be placed on the metal bracket. The research can offer references for studying on spacecraft surface charging effect in ground study.

articleTitle: A novel multifunctional quadrature hybrid coupler
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A new multifunctional quadrature coupler is proposed and developed at 2.0 GHz, with a 70.7% wide operating band, good frequency selectivity, and high harmonic suppression over 30 dB at 6.0 GHz. It is realized with EBG-/DGS-loaded arms and open-ended coupled lines. With the properly selected critical parameters, arbitrary power division ratio, such as 2:1, can easily be achieved. The measured and simulated results agree well with each other, which demonstrate our idea. A compact prototype is developed with the occupied area of 48.0×21.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A beam-switchable dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The paper proposes a new beam-switchable dipole antenna. The functionability is realized by reconfiguring the state of the four side apertures of a square substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). Four wide dipoles are loaded in front of the four apertures. The selected radiating aperture is able to excite the corresponding loaded dipole. The other dipoles work as reflectors. Thus, directional radiation patterns can be obtained in each state. Owning to its symmetrical structure, the proposed antenna is capable of switching the radiation beam every 90° with identical radiation patterns in the H-plane. An impedance bandwidth of approximately 50% for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB is achieved with an antenna gain of approximately 4.3 dBi for each state.

articleTitle: Scan-ISAR imaging for translational motion targets
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The cross-range resolution of Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) image is highly dependent on the relative motion between radar and observed targets, in which the rotational motion can induce different Doppler modulation for different scatterers. However, in practice there exists only translational motion of target. In this paper, a scan-ISAR imaging algorithm for translational motion targets is proposed, where the thought that synthetic aperture is accomplished by the rotation of antenna. Experimental results have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on the design techniques of Hilbert frad pattern ground shield
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The lack of high performance on-chip spiral inductor is one of the key factors hindering the miniaturization of integrated circuit. In this paper, the Hilbert fractal pattern ground shield has been designed to suppress eddy current loss, and improve the spiral element quality factor based on HHNEC 1P6M BiCMOS process. Result of electromagnetic simulation shows that about 24% improvement in the Q-peak (13/2.5 GHz) of novel technique single inductor as compared to conventional single inductors (10.5/1.6 GHz), and about 8.3% improvement in the Q-peak as compared to strip pattern ground shield inductors (12/1.8 GHz).

articleTitle: A design of dual-band circularly polarized microstrip antenna with single feed on one single layer substrate
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A simple structure dual-band circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna (MSA) installed on a single layer substrate is designed in this paper. The slotted radiation patch with four symmetric stubs of this MSA is fed by a coaxial line. The MSA has good CP characteristics and impedance matching in both of the two bands. Moreover, we can easily get different frequency ratio of the higher and lower center frequency (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(fH/fL)</sub>) by adjusting the dimensions and positions of the slots and the dimensions of the stubs on the patch. The bandwidth of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>≤-10dB can be achieved 3.4% and 2.2% respectively for lower and upper frequency band and the bandwidth of axial ratio (AR) less than 3dB is about 20MHz for both bands. The radiation pattern performance is right hand circular polarization (RHCP) in this design and the co-polarization gain is larger than 6.5dBic.

articleTitle: A broadband dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel wideband dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole unidirectional antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of dual-layer magneto-electric (ME)-dipole and two Γ-shaped probes. Its two ports both achieve a common impedance bandwidth of 91.6%(SWR<2). The antenna has excellent performance in isolation, which is more than 15dB, and a high front-to-back ration more than 14.8dB over the operating band.

articleTitle: A dual-band slot antenna design using particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A dual-band printed slot antenna designed and optimized by particle swarm optimization for wireless local area network operation has been proposed in this study. The proposed antenna consists of folded dual slots operated at the half-wavelength mode and a T-shaped strip which excites the dual slots. The optimized antenna has a compact substrate size of 40.0 mm by 15.0 mm only. Optimized results show that the proposed antenna covers the WLAN operating bands at 2.45 GHz (2.4 GHz-2.484 GHz) and 5.25 GHz (5.15-5.35 GHz).

articleTitle: Research on online signal matching of indoor positioning based on AL-KNN algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Considering the factors of environmental adaptability, laying cost and system complexity, the signal fingerprint positioning based on RFID systems has become a better choice of the positioning technology. Online and offline signal matching technology is very important stage for the signal fingerprint positioning. In this paper, we propose a signal matching algorithm in order to further improve the positioning accuracy. This new algorithm is modified version of k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). As the fluctuation of signal strength, the variance of data set as a characteristic is selected. In order to make full use of offline fingerprint information, we constitute a new k-l nearest neighbor collection, not just k nearest neighbor collection of KNN. The simulation results prove this proposed algorithm can effectively improve the positioning accuracy compared with the other traditional algorithm.

articleTitle: Wideband Fabry-Perot Cavity antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain low-profile Fabry-Perot Cavity antenna with a wide 3-dB gain bandwidth is proposed. By employing a gradually increased wedge structure on the ground, the 3-dB gain bandwidth is improved from 17% to 24.2%. Moreover, this structure has almost no influences on the impedance bandwidth and the maximum realized gain of the Fabry-Perot cavity antenna.

articleTitle: A RCS prediction method for multipath effect of the ground plane
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A radar cross section (RCS) prediction method for multipath effect of the ground plane is presented in this paper. In this paper, the scattering contribution is constructed by four parts: the direct wave, the ground clutter, and two bistatic paths due to the ground reflection. Each part of the contribution is calculated independently. By synthesizing the four parts, the total scattering field of the ground target system is obtained. Several numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Coding phase gradient metasurface: Simultaneous modulation of coding elements and coding sequences
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A new way to design coding phase gradient metasurface (CPGM) is proposed in this work. Different from the previous CPGM, the modulation of coding elements and coding sequences can be achieved simultaneously. Thus, the manipulations of electromagnetic (EM) wave will be more flexible for CPGMs. As an example, CPGMs with and without modulation of coding elements are achieved. The co-polarization reflection unit cells under circularly polarized (CP) wave incidence are considered to constitute the coding elements based on Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase. The simulated scattering patterns of the designed CPGMs demonstrate the expected manipulations.

articleTitle: A Schottky diodes based W-band 4th-harmonic mixer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband fourth-harmonic mixer based on gallium arsenide (GaAs) Schottky barrier diodes working at 80–100GHz is designed. This fourth-harmonic mixer is simulated and attains low conversion loss below 14dB in the whole band. The design process and simulation results are explained in detail.

articleTitle: Low side-lobe substrate integrated cavity antenna array using unequal microstrip-ridge gap waveguide feeding network at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a 4×32 low side-lobe slot antenna array using unequal microstrip-ridge gap waveguide (GWG) feeding network at 94 GHz is presented. The slot antenna array is built by two double-sided printed circuit boards (PCBs). The top one employs SIW-based 2×2 subarrays and the bottom one is a broadband 2×16 way unequal GWG feeding network. Applying Taylor amplitude weighting in the 16 way GWG feeding network, low side-lobe performance is achieved. The unequal T-junction dividers with phase compensation are proposed and designed for various output ratios. Simulated results show that the antenna array achieves 5 GHz bandwidth with a peak gain of 26.3 dBi at 94 GHz. Across the entire band, low side lobe level (SLL) below −20 dB is realized.

articleTitle: Folded reflectarray antennas based on diagonal slots patches
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Folded reflectarray antennas can provide a good solution for millimeter-wave systems requiring compact, low-cost antennas, e.g. in automotive applications. A rectangular patch with diagonal slots in the edges is investigated and found to present a phase angle range of more than 460° due to the two resonances. The novel antenna achieves higher gain and better performance, compared to a reflectarray with simple rectangular elements.

articleTitle: The theoretical analysis on electromagnetic signal transmission for down-hole to surface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Based on the equivalent source and NMM (numerical mode matching method), the theory model method of electromagnetic signal transmission for down-hole to surface by is established. The gap antenna and toroid were calculated, the influence of the input impedance and of incentive to drill string current is analyzed, through calculation and comparison that the gap antenna method is more suitable for the electromagnetic signal transmission for down-hole to surface.

articleTitle: Analysis of power frequency interference when the single end of the sensor circuit is grounded
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to analyze the problem of signal power frequency interference when the single end of the sensor is connected to the ground. The circuit model of the power frequency crosstalk voltage on the core wire is established. The electromagnetic field distribution around the shielding layer is analyzed base on the finite element software ANSYS. And the calculation formula of crosstalk voltage on cable and the measures to reduce crosstalk voltage are presented.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional ISAR imaging based on amplitude and phase errors correction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: InISAR imaging systems generally employ a multi-antenna pair model with orthogonal properties. In practical applications, there may be amplitude and phase errors in different antenna receiving channels, and the obtained ISAR target echo signal also has errors. Although several algorithms have been proposed, these algorithms can only work with no amplitude and phase error. This paper proposed an algorithm to achieve three-dimensional ISAR imaging based on the channels with amplitude and phase errors. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has good performance.

articleTitle: Compact W-band antipodal fin-line transition from SIW to rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact wideband transition realized by inserting triangular antipodal fin-line probe into metallic rectangular waveguide from substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is presented. One back-to-back transition covering a bandwidth of 20 GHz in W band is designed, fabricated and tested to show the advantages of such antipodal fin line-probe inspired transition structure, and the measured results consist well with the simulations. An insertion loss less than 2 dB and a return loss better than 15 dB over 86-106 GHz are obtained for the back-to-back structure. The proposed broadband triangular fin-line transition can be used widely in microwave and millimeter-wave circuit and system.

articleTitle: A conical conformal circularly polarized microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A circularly polarized microstrip antenna installed on the surface of a cone is proposed in this paper. The radiation patch with a pair of crossed slot conformal on the conical surface is fed by a coaxial line and the antenna has a good circularly polarized characteristics and impedance matching by adjusting the length of the crossed slot and the feed position. This antenna is working on GPS and Beidou (BD) satellite communication at the same time. Its bandwidth of VSWR≤2 can be achieved 6.8% around 1.568GHz, and the radiation pattern performance is right hand circular polarization (RHCP). The axial ratio is lower than 4dB and the RHCP Gain is larger than 4dBic at both bands of 1.561GHz for BD and 1.575GHz for GPS.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of a compact and broadband antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel compact broadband antenna is proposed in this letter. This idea is based on the traditional antenna printed dipole which is applied in many areas. The proposed antenna is consisted of microstrip barron line, ground plane, two oscillator arms and an inverted-L-shape feeder. This antenna is smaller compared to the conventional antenna, but it can reach the better performance. Through the simulation of the antenna, the return loss reaches 18.61%. The proposed antenna has advantages of light, small and low cost.

articleTitle: Magnetically tunable metamaterial absorber based on cube ferrite
