By comparing with the questionnaire results, it is shown that the proposed method can provide more accurate evaluation than a previous method called Mean Equivalent Area Method.

articleTitle: Planar two-arm spiral antenna fed by microstrip line
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A planar microstrip-fed two-arm spiral antenna has been designed for achieving wideband circularly polarized bandwidth in this paper. Compared with conventional spiral antennas, a simple feeding line is employed to feed the antenna. The planar structure can be printed using a single layer substrate without an external balun. In addition, the arc-shaped cut is embedded in the ground plane and a tapered impedance transformer is utilized to improve the impedance matching across a wide frequency band. The obtained results confirm that the proposed antenna can achieve a circularly polarized bandwidth from 2 to 4 GHz with the peak realized gain varying from 2 to 3.7 dBi.

articleTitle: A compact low-profile C-band dual circularly polarized sub-array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact low-profile cavity-backed dual circularly polarized (CP) sub-array antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed C-band antenna array has a 2×2-element microstrip patch antenna. The operating bandwidth of the proposed antenna is ranging from 0.89f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 1.11f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (about 22%) with the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 2, where the f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is center frequency of the target band. Moreover, the axial ratio (AR) is less than 3 dB for the entire desired band. The highlight of this proposed antenna is that it can realize dual circularly polarized radiation with a compact structure. In addition, the depth of the cavity is only about λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/8. The detailed structure and simulated results of the proposed dual CP sub-array antenna will be presented.

articleTitle: Combination of MLFMA and ACA to accelerate computation of scattering from underground pipelines
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to detect pipelines underground to avoid accidents in urban construction, ground penetrating radar (GPR) is applied for non-destructive evaluation. Surface integral equations are used to model the scattering properties of the underground pipes and method of moment (MoM) is used to solve the equations. Since both multi-level fast multi-pole algorithm (MLFMA) and adaptive cross approximation (ACA) method can extremely accelerate the efficient of moment method, a hybrid scheme by combing the two methods together is proposed to accelerate the calculation of scattering from underground pipes. The self-interaction of the earth or underground geometries is accelerated by MLFMA. The coupling between earth and pipes is accelerated by ACA. Numerical results show the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study on the spatial distribution of electromagnetic scattering characteristics of radar targets
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: It is important to study the spatial distribution of electromagnetic scattering characteristics of radar targets. This paper is based on the bistatic scattering data, analysis of target scattering characteristics in spatial domain, gives the calculation formula of the total power of target scattering, and the calculated data were analyzed.

articleTitle: The applications of jumping genes inspired evolutionary algorithms in microwave circuit designs
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The optimization of a microwave circuit is a complex multi-objective problem (MOP) needed to be effectively solved. Multi-objective evolution algorithms (MOEAs) are efficient in dealing with MOPs because of their population property inspired by the natural evolution of species. Exploitation and exploration are of equal importance to MOEAs for approximating the optimal Pareto front (PF) well. However, most of them are focus on exploitation, and may result in poor diversity or stick at local optimal front. Jumping genes operator (JG) inspired from a biological discovery was introduced in different evolutionary algorithms to maintain the balance between in convergence and diversity. In this paper, the principle, applications and future directions for jumping genes inspired evolutionary algorithm are summarized.

articleTitle: Comparison of three different methods for terrain modeling in parabolic equation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the parabolic equation model applied to irregular terrain is solved by using the split-step Fourier transform algorithm under the perfectly conducting condition. The forecast of propagation over irregular terrain is presented by using the terrain-masking model, the boundary-shift method, the shift map, and the piecewise linear shift map respectively, where the shift map is adopted as a standard for validation. The average error and standard deviation between the shift map solution and the other three methods are analyzed, which provides a theoretical support for the selection of terrain models in the actual situation.

articleTitle: The performance studies of passive anti-metal UHF RFID tag in substation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We analyze the performance of anti-metal tags when they work in EMC (Electro Magnetic Compatibility) chamber and in substation. It is meaningful to the promotion of RFID(Radio Frequency Identification) tags applied in substation.

articleTitle: Analysis of broadband near zero index metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Based on a broadband near-zero refractive index metamaterial, the unit structure is simulated by electromagnetic software HFSS, and its reflection-transmission parameters are extracted. And the classical inversion algorithm is used to derive the band in the 16-17.5GHz with the same permeability and permittivity. However, the effect of near zero effect is not ideal and the refractive index is zero is not shown.

articleTitle: A review of advanced characteristic mode theories for complex electromagnetic problems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Characteristic mode (CM) theory is widely used nowadays for analysis and design of radiation and scattering problems. In this paper, we discuss the recent developments of advanced characteristic mode theory and its applications in complex electromagnetic (EM) problems. Following the deep physical insights into the radiation and scattering mechanisms of complex electromagnetic open problems, the effective use of CM allows antenna designs and scattering control in a systematic way. This is also what the latest progress of advanced CM theory developments made at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) can really benefit the EM community.

articleTitle: Planar lens antenna based on low-pass frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A planar lens antenna based on low-pass frequency selective surfaces is presented in this paper. The presented lens operates at 1.7-2.2GHz and shows a low-profile structure with an overall thickness of 0.2 operating wavelength. A dipole antenna array is used as the feed. The simulation results show that the antenna presents high aperture efficiency and the gain reaches 17.69dBi. The scanning beam within a range of ±30° is achieved.

articleTitle: Research on parallel space mapping algorithm for filter design
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Space mapping algorithm is an effective method to speed up optimization. Automatic optimization of space mapping algorithm is realized in this paper. Parallel multi-machine simulation technology is utilized to enhance the calculation efficiency. A microwave low-pass filter is optimized using the proposed algorithm. The efficiency is improved by about forty percent and it provides a new technical way for design of complex microwave components and antennas.

articleTitle: Application of near-field target characteristic in missile-target encounter simulation for fuse
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of fuse's digital simulation in Missile-target Encounter, an algorithm based on PO and PTD and GO methods is presented for calculating the echo characteristics of fuse, including pulse echo power and signal and the near-field RCS. Numerical results prove the proposed method high efficiency. It would be especially valuable in engineering application.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental comparison of radiation near-fields of BWS with distributed terminator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Based on iterative expressions of Uniaxial anisotropic Perfectly Matched Layer(UPML) absorbing boundary for media with magnetic loss, a symmetrical method, combined with parallelized Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method and perfect magnetic conductor(PMC) boundary condition, is presented in this paper. The examples of Bounded wave simulator(BWS) with distributed terminator are given. The results agree well with those of normal FDTD, and computing time is saved. The comparison of simulation with experiment is also offered. The method shown in this paper is universal for other BWS and antennas with symmetric tangential fields.

articleTitle: Design of omni-directional cavity backed antenna for aerocraft application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An omni-directional cavity backed antenna is proposed this paper. The antenna is used for space aerocraft, so the cavity backed antenna is “buried” in the platform to ensure the good fluid mechanics characters. A simple monopole is used here for good omni-direction radiation and to enlarge the radiation in the low elevation angle, a conical cavity is used. A dielectric filled gap between the conical cavity and platform is adopted here to reduce the platform effect and also the heat conduction to the antenna. The simulated and measured results are given, which show good performances of this antenna.

articleTitle: Calculator of WPT efficiency between transmitting and receiving elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An universal approach to calculate the transfer efficiency between arbitrary transmitting and receiving elements has been proposed so for. The approach makes using of either S-parameter or Z-parameter. In this paper, firstly, the efficiency calculation method will be reviewed briefly, and then the functions of the developed calculator will be introduced.

articleTitle: Characterization of antenna voltage standing wave ratio under plasma sheath
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The plasma sheath around the surface of hypersonic vehicle causes the mismatching of antenna impedance. As a result, it leads to the change of antenna voltage standing wave ratio(VSWR). The purpose of this paper is to investigate the characteristics of VSWR on a GPS right-hand circularly polarized patch antenna. The results demonstrate that VSWR is largely influenced with the electron density and the collision frequency. In addition, the strong negative correlation between VSWR and the transmission loss can support the idea that channel performance can be predicted by monitoring the change of VSWR. Furthermore, the mean electron density under a certain thickness of sheath can be estimated using the theory of equivalent transmission lines. Above all, all these characteristics on VSWR lay a solid theoretical foundation of diagnosing the parameters of plasma sheath.

articleTitle: Automated EM-level design framework for sequential coupled resonator filters
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An efficient fully automated EM-level design framework is implemented using Matlab, Sonnetlab toolbox and Sonnet EM simulator for the design of different type of sequentially coupled resonator planar filters. The proposed implementation integrates the space mapping technique and reflected group delay method to achieve fast and reliable EM-based filter design. In this paper, two design examples are given to validate the performance of the proposed design framework.

articleTitle: Signal distortion compensation based on a two-prot negative impedance convertor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We construct a two-port non-Foster element with an unconventional use of a floating negative impedance convertor. Compared with one-port non-Foster elements, it is able to have a non-Foster transmission coefficient that can be used to compensate distortion of input signals due to nonlinear frequency response of Foster networks. Both theoretical and simulated analysis verified the effectiveness of the proposed element.

articleTitle: Advanced modeling of characteristic mode theory for antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper is to share and review recent development of characteristic mode (CM) theory and its applications, including CM theory based optimization, CM theory for simple antenna design, CM theory for integrated structural antenna design, CM theory for dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) design, and CM theory for layered medium structures.

articleTitle: Broadband circularly polarized antenna for global navigation satellite system combined receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A broadband right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) global navigation satellite system (GNSS) antenna is proposed to cover global positioning system (GPS), GLONASS, Galileo and Compass applications. The -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth is fully covered all of the GNSS bands. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 475 MHz from 1.175 to 1.65 GHz. The gain is above 0 dBi from 1.22 to 1.65 GHz. Therefore the proposed antenna can cover the frequency range from GPS L2 band to GLONASS L1 band. Simulated results indicate that the proposed antenna can be used in navigation devices of multiple GNSSs.

articleTitle: Design of low phase noise oscillator employing substrate integrated waveguide filter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact low phase noise oscillator based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) structure is presented. The oscillator employs a third-degree cross-coupled bandpass SIW filter as the frequency stabilization element. Meanwhile, the groupdelay and the complex quality factor (Qsc) are all taken into consideration for the oscillator design, which is more accurate than the traditional method. The measured phase noise performance of the developed oscillator is −112.9 dBc/Hz at 100 KHz offset frequency and the figure of merit (FOM) at 100KHz is −201.65 dBc/Hz with high output power of 8.9 dBm at 12.22 GHz.

articleTitle: A high gain ultra-wideband microstrip antenna based on metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high gain ultrawideband microstrip antenna based on metamaterial structure. The designed antenna consists of a rectangle radiation patch etched T-shaped slots on the top layer, a ground plane with crossed shaped slots on the bottom layer and is fed by a 50 Ω microstrip line, the total size is 28 mm×2 mm, the thickness is 0.8 mm. The simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 4.0 GHz to 16.2 GHz with S11 less than −10 dB, which is about 120.8% broader. The gains of designed antenna are all higher than 6 dBi, and they higher than 8 dBi at the most of working band. Thus, this antenna would be a good candidate for UWB wireless communications in the future.

articleTitle: Topology optimization of microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Two topology optimization methods, namely material distribution and level-set methods, are used for optimization of microstrip antennas. By successive application of the two methods, the optimization process can take advantage of the powerful topology-searching ability of the material distribution method and the feature of generating structures with smooth and low-sensitivity boundaries of level-set method. This two-stage optimization scheme is used in the design of three microstrip antennas. All the antennas are fabricated and measured. Measured data show that all the antennas achieve desirable performances, as prescribed by objective functions, in reflection, polarization and beam pattern.

articleTitle: A high resolution radar range profile simulator for low flying target above sea surface with multipath effect
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: To theoretically evaluate multipath effect on radar characteristics of low flying target. This letter presents an applicable method in description of multipath coupling between target and ocean surface. It illustrates a composite scale scattering description over physically modelled ocean surface. Then it introduces a facet-based imaging thought in coupling consideration. The method is well suitable in application of the multipath evaluation in electrically large scale scenes and has the advantage to reflect both specular and diffuse scattering effects over complex surface profile. The HRRP simulation results are also presented and discussed, which show multipath effect clearly.

articleTitle: Analytical solutions for near-field light scattering by a metal nanospheroid
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The near-field analytical solutions for light scattering by metal nanospheroids are presented by solving Maxwell's equations in spheroidal coordinate using the separation of variables method (SVM). Based on the vector spheroidal wave functions (VSWFs), the expressions for the internal and the scattered fields are derived analytically. Then the effectiveness and correctness of the method are verified in two ways, first the radar cross sections (RCS) values are compared with those computed by Mie theory in the case of small eccentricity, and second the RCS results for prolate case are compared with those calculated by the finite element method (FEM). In both cases the RCS values coincide very well. To give a further validation, we plot the near-field distributions of silver nanospheroids using SVM and FEM simulations, respectively. Good agreements are also observed. Then the optical excitations of localized plasmon resonances are analyzed by calculating the extinction efficiency, and plotting the near-field distributions under the resonance condition. The electric field enhancement in the near-field region is shown to be sufficiently large.

articleTitle: Designs of miniaturized differential bandpass filters using dual-mode dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, two types of dual-mode dielectric resonators (DRs) are utilized to design miniaturized differential bandpass filters (BPFs). According to the boundary conditions of the electromagnetic fields, inserting a metal plate on the electric field's symmetry plane doesn't disturb the original field distributions. Thus, the structure of each employed DR is introduced by cutting off along the electric field's symmetry plane and inserting a metal plate on the section, resulting in significant size reduction compared with the conventional one. Meanwhile, a pair of orthogonal half-cut modes of each dual-mode DR can be differentially excited and coupled for constructing the differential-mode (DM) passband of differential dual-mode DR BPF. For demonstration, two differential BPFs employing the proposed dual-mode DRs are designed and simulated, showing good DM and common-mode (CM) responses as well as offering a significant size reduction in comparison with the conventional differential filters.

articleTitle: Accurate and efficient simulation of plasmonic bubbles produced by light illumination
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPR) give rise to enhanced fields near the interface between the metallic and dielectric boundary. Strong excitation intensities can lead to the formation of photothermal bubbles around plasmonic nanoparticles. Numerical simulation is indispensable in predicting and analyzing plasmonic bubble as the measurement is always too expensive or too complicated to be carried out. This work reports our work in computing the plasmonic bubble phenomenon.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo worst case analysis of atom probe tomography microelectrode
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The electrode constitutes the key element of the atom probe (AP) pulse signal generator. The AP parameter Monte Carlo (MC) analysis is introduced. The AP microelectrode is designed with 50-Ω loaded microstrip line centered by via hole. The excitation square wave pulse presents 300-ps duration and 1-kV amplitude. The worst cases of the signal integrity is performed with MC analysis applied to the electrode transmission line metallization width sensitivity. Computation results with commercial frequency analysis from DC to 10-GHz is presented. The worst-case analysis is necessary for the AP performance optimization by increasing the radiated pulsed electric-field.

articleTitle: Least squares estimation of formation bedding orientation from electromagnetic measurements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: One of the challenging aspects in directional electromagnetic measurements is to accurately estimate the formation bedding orientation angle, which is critical to help maintain drilling the wellbore in the sweetest spots of the reservoir. Various existing methods can be both noisy and susceptible to phase wrapping issues. Here we present a new approach for accurately computing the bedding orientation angle, based on least squares technique applied to the acquired voltages. It successfully avoids the phase wrapping issues. Moreover, the angle is computed by minimizing the weighted sum of squared residuals of acquired voltages, which provides more accurate angle estimation owing to a robust mathematic model. This novel approach has been well validated with a large number of cases. The results demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the method.

articleTitle: A phase quantization method to improve the beam pointing accuracy of the phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a phase quantization method named appropriate recursive comparative compensation method (ARCCM) is presented. ARCCM develops on the basis of recursive comparative compensation method (RCCM) using the phased array antenna virtual bit technology (VBT). In allusion to one-dimensional uniform linear array, ARCCM is analyzed and simulated. Compared with other methods, the beam pointing accuracy of the phased array antenna obviously improves by using ARCCM, especially when large angle beam scanning.

articleTitle: Extension of 3GPP 3-dimensional channel models for large-scale parameters in the gymnasium scenario
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As an important scenario for indoor coverage, the space-time characteristics of the wireless channels inside a gymnasium are investigated in this paper. By using a 3-dimensional sounder with two crossed, dual-polarized linear antenna arrays, the large-scale parameters (LSPs) such as root-mean-square azimuth/zenith spread of arrival (ASA/ZSA), delay spread (DS), and Rician K factor of the channels from audience areas to tops of stands were measured. It is found that their empirical distributions follow the log-normal PDFs well. The cross-correlation coefficients among the LSPs are calculated, some of which are lack in the 3GPP specification. The autocorrelation distances which indicate the spatial variation of the parameters are also analyzed. The presented results can extend the current 3D channel models and support the deployment of small cells in the indoor hot-spot scenario.

articleTitle: Pattern reconfigurable antenna with flowing liquid switch
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new solution for realizing a pattern reconfigurable dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) using liquid injection to the 3D-printed container. The proposed methodology solves the existing problems of PIN-diode type reconfigurable antennas in narrow bandwidth and low radiation efficiency. The proposed DRA successfully demonstrates how to manipulate HEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> modes with broadside and conical patterns in two states.

articleTitle: MIMO radar images of a trihedral corner reflector for near-field measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar is of great research interest in recent years. The impacts of inherent bistatic geometry of a MIMO array on target images might be severe at short distances. This is due to the fact that each virtual element synthesized by a MIMO array cannot be considered as a mono-static transmit/receive element. In this paper, we study the characteristics of near-field MIMO images for a trihedral corner reflector like scattering mechanism which is sensitive to bistatic measurement geometry.

articleTitle: Integrated CT sigma-delta modulator and LNA with WuRx antenna for wireless tracheostomy tube
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This article presents the design and experimental results of a continuous-time (CT) sigma-delta (ΣΔ) flexible modulator and low noise amplifier (LNA) with data-weighted average (DWA) technology. An image-reject low noise amplifier is designed for wireless tracheostomy tube and bio-signal acquisitions. An inter-stage T-structure filter is used in the low noise amplifier design to bending antenna. The DWA technique is used for reducing DAC noise due to component mismatches. This proposed wireless sensor setup CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> concentration detecting instruments on chip. Oxygen generator will real time to support as sensor monitor and wireless send bio-signal to health center.

articleTitle: Wideband microstrip endfire antenna based on SIW and magnetic dipole
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A wideband microstrip endfire antenna is designed for applications in base station and satellite communication. Utilizing substrate integrated waveguide technology, vertically polarized wave is generated by the driven element of the antenna. And a parasitic microstrip patch with one edge opened and the other three edges shorted is introduced as the magnetic dipole to improve the impedance matching and enhance the gain in low elevation angular domain. The measured results indicate that the proposed antenna exhibits 44.4% fractional bandwidth from 9.8 to 15.4 GHz, and moderate gain of 6.53~8.14 dBi.

articleTitle: Verify microstrip antenna using feature selective verification method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The Feature Selective Validation (FSV) Method has been developed as a standard technique to mimic an expert's opinion of concurrence between computational electromagnetics (CEM) and measurement datasets. In this paper, FSV is used to compare the design simulation and measurement of the microstrip antenna to verify the difference between the simulation data and the measured data. First, a typical patch antenna model is constructed from design experience. Secondly, the electromagnetic simulation of the antenna model is carried out using the electromagnetic simulation software, and the S-parameters simulation data are obtained. Finally, the electromagnetic simulation data and measured data of the microstrip antenna model are compared and verified by the FSV method, which shows the effectiveness of the microstrip design under investigating.

articleTitle: A hybrid method for EMI effect simulation of cable-interconnect network
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid method for electromagnetic interference (EMI) analysis of braid cable-interconnect network. In this method, the full-wave finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD) and transmission line equation are combined to predict the transient responses of cable-interconnect networks. Transfer impedance model is introduced as connection conditions so that the external field can be applied by way of adding incentive items into the transmission line equations. This method has good agreements with HSPICE. Finally, the method is used in analyzing a cable-interconnect network with different shielding characteristics.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave control based on tunable graphene property
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With graphene emerging as one of the promising materials in exploring novel and reconfigurable electromagnetic devices, in this paper, we summarize and discuss the electromagnetic property of graphene in different frequencies, as well as introduced two kinds of, namely, surface-wave and spatial-wave based electromagnetic devices base on graphene. Simultaneously, typical mechanisms for designing these devices are provided in brief.

articleTitle: A dense monopole array for spatial noise shaping
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A dense sleeve monopole antenna array is proposed for improving the noise figure (NF) and linearity of array receivers via spatial delta-sigma (Δ-Σ) noise shaping. The planar array has a spatial oversampling ratio of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> = 4. The shared ground-shorted sleeves were optimized for low mutual coupling (less than −10 dB between adjacent monopoles). Simulated and experimental results for the proposed design are discussed. The measured element radiation pattern is omnidirectional in the H-plane and has a peak gain of −5 dBi, which is in good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Design of spatial filter applied to millimeter wave fast imaging system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In millimeter wave imaging system especially millimeter wave holographic imaging system, image quality relies heavily on the accuracy of measured signal. A spatial filter for fast millimeter wave imaging system is designed to acquire more accurate data. More importantly, integration of the spatial filter into the imaging system would significantly relax strict requirements on transceivers. System complexity and cost might be accordingly reduced.

articleTitle: The way from natural to artificial — The story of periodic electromagnetic structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the general of artificial electromagnetic structure with analog to the natural materials were briefly reviewed. The lattice theory of artificial structure was suggested to be built.

articleTitle: Investigation of the related factors of angle measurements precision in monopulse radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Angle measurement of monopulse is widely used in the angle tracing technique for high precision tracking radar system. This paper analyzes some facts related with precision of angle measurements in monopulse radar, including offset angle of sub-beams, squint angle between target and centerline of main beam, receiver output noise, and target amplitude fluctuation. A new method for angle measurement of monopulse, which is based on digital beam forming technology, is investigated in the paper to achieve angle measurement of monopulse radar. The results show that, receiver output noise and squint angle between target and centerline of main beam, which are two important factors affecting precision of angle measurements in monopulse radar.

articleTitle: Ultrabroadband polarization-insensitive far-infrared metameterial absorber by gold nanowire array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-broadband polarization-insensitive far-infrared metamterial absorber with gold nanowire is proposed. Unlike some traditional metamaterial absorbers consisting of multilayer structure, our design is made up of gold nanowire array which is much simpler. Height and permittivity constant gradient both contribute to the broadband absorption. Each single gold nanowire acts as a nano-resonator, an array of nanowires with different height and dielectric together realize ultrabroadband absorption. In addition, our design could be extended to any other frequency regimes, which indicates potential applications in infrared detection, imaging and so on.

articleTitle: Modeling of an uncooled CMOS THz thermal detector with frequency-selective loop antenna and NMOS temperature sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a thermal THz detector based on commercial CMOS technology working at room temperature consisting of a loop antenna and a NMOS temperature sensor. The THz electromagnetic wave is absorbed by the loop antenna at first, then the absorbed energy is converted into heat via a resistor. The temperature rise of the resistor is finally detected by a NMOS temperature sensor. The physical modeling of the detector including the electromagnetic energy absorption, the thermal conversion and the electrical circuit response.

articleTitle: Long-distance geomagetic navigation based on the simulation of Animals' migration
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The methods and mechanisms behind Animals' cross-continental migration is still a mystery up to now. Researchers from different backgrounds have done large amounts of work trying to throw light on this puzzle. In this work, methods different from all the previous researches are used to investigate animal navigation. Combined with natural cues that animals rely on, a navigation algorithm based on geomagnetic spatial angle is proposed to simulate animals' navigation behaviors. Our results not only match existing observation reports, but are also able to explain some conflicting evidences on the role of geomagnetic field in animal navigation.

articleTitle: Research on anti-jamming technology of conformal array based on beamforming
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An iterative least-squares (RLS) anti-jamming technique is applied to a conformal antenna for improving the adaptive anti-jamming performance. This method offers a solution to synthesize predefined radiation pattern. By iterative calculation, a set of constraint weights of linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) can be obtained to improve the adaptive nulling depth and to expand the angle coverage of the conformal array beam.

articleTitle: A probe-fed stacked U-slot patch antena for satellite applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A probe-fed stacked U-slot patch antenna for satellite applications is presented. The impedance bandwidth (VSWR≤1.5) of 7.7% is achieved at the designed frequency fo. The simulated peak realized gain of the proposed antenna is about 9 dBi.

articleTitle: Efficient motion compensation of moving targets in SAR imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A procedure is presented to retrieve motion parameters of the moving target from single-channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data in a long-time coherent integration, and make motion compensation for SAR imaging. Firstly, the slant-range velocity is estimated using Radon transform which is not affected by the Doppler ambiguity, and after correcting the range walk induced by the slant-range motion, the target energy can be concentrated into a single range cell. Then, accurate motion compensation can be made efficiently via the velocity correlation function (VCF) based algorithm. The typical experimental result for simulated SAR data demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Compact micro strip diplexer based on resonators with adjustable frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel small planar micro strip diplexer is presented for Long-Term Evolution (LTE) System at 1.8 GHz and 2.6 GHz. The proposed structure consist ring shaped resonators. Changing the size of the ring resonators relate to change of the resonant frequencies. These resonators and stubs decrease the size of the structures, owing to adding the inductive and capacitive effects of the structure and also used to tune coupling between resonators. The measured results show two near frequency channels (centered at 1.8GHz and 2.6GHz) with isolation more than 25 dB. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Design of controlling circuit for varactor diodes based on K-band pattern reconfigurable antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A controlling circuit for varactor diodes based on K-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) leaky-wave antenna is presented in this paper to accomplish pattern reconfiguration. The varactors' DC bias is supplied by a sawtooth wave generated from the FPGA which allows automatic and continuous variation of the capacitance of the varactors. An isolating circuit between DC voltage and RF is applied to the antenna to make it work properly. Consequently, a design of pattern reconfigurable antenna is accomplished and beam scanning is detected from 21GHz to 23GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a miniaturized ultra-wideband antenna with U-shape slots
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A miniaturized UWB microstrip antenna is proposed in this letter. The microstrip antenna with a compact size of 28 mm × 37mm × 1.59 mm is composed of a metal patch with double nested U-shape slots and double nested inverted-U-shape slots, a dielectric slab and a ground plate with double inverted-L-shape slots. The proposed antenna has been designed using FR4 as a substrate with dielectric constant of 4.4. The antenna is fed by a microstrip line of 50 Ω. The Ansoft HFSS simulation results show that the relative bandwidth of the antenna is 71.5% and the bandwidth is from 6.41GHz to 13.56GHz for S11 ≤ -10 dB.

articleTitle: Statistical research on RCSR performance of random phase metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a statistical research is carried on the radar cross section reduction (RCSR) performance of diffuse metasurface composed of two-layer stacked-patch elements. The research focuses on the broadband RCSR behavior of the metasurface in specular direction. An advanced uniform random distribution of reflection phase is proposed for the diffuse metasurface to improve the broadband RCSR performance in a statistical sense.

articleTitle: A novel compact dual polarized spiral feed for reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A double-layer, two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna is investigated as a feed in reflector antennas with circularly polarized rims. A kind of compact spiral antennas with center-fed and a planar reflector as a ground plane are studied. Both right- and left-handed circularly polarized fields with broadside radiation patterns can be acquired. This proposed feed exhibits excellent pattern symmetry and axial ratios at the boresight direction for both senses of polarization. In this letter, the performance of the proposed spiral antenna is fully addressed as primary feeds in symmetrical parabolic reflector antennas. Excellent VSWR and radiation patterns are obtained over a frequency band of 1.08-1.42 GHz.

articleTitle: Automated topology optimization of internal antenna design using improved BPSO
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes an automated topology optimization technique for internal antenna design using an improved BPSO. A new transfer function with a time-variant transfer factor is proposed to improve the problem of easily falling into local optimum in conventional BPSO. Compact tri-band planar antenna design is presented, showing that the proposed technique significantly outperforms the previous topology optimizations.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable graphene transmission array for the generation of vortex THz waves
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable graphene transmission array is proposed for the generation of vortex radio waves at THz. By perforating the substrate with holes of various diameters, different values of effective permittivity are obtained. The transmission coefficient can be adjusted by changing the chemical potential of graphene. With the excitation of planar wave, the phase-compensation of corresponding regions will create multimode orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves. Numerical example shows that the proposed graphene transmission array can be reconfigured to generate and transform the 0, 1, 2 modes of vortex radio wave at 2.0 THz.

articleTitle: Polarimetrie passive millimeter wave image fusion based on NSCT
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A polarimetric passive millimeter wave image fusion method is proposed based on Nonsubsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT) in this paper. The NSCT is initially applied to decompose the polarimetric passive millimeter wave images into low-frequency and high-frequency subbands, and the sparse representation and average weighted method are employed as the fusion rules for low-frequency and high-frequency subbands respectively to realize the fusion of polarimetric passive millimeter wave images. The fusion performances are evaluated with several metrics. The experimental results show that the fused image obtained by the proposed method has a better visual and quantitative performance than the original images.

articleTitle: Performance comparsion among different objective functions in paramter estimation of scattering center
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As the advantages of good convergence and less computing time in estimating multiple parameters, genetic algorithm (GA) has been applied to estimate the parameters of the multiple scattering centers. It is found that various objective functions (OF) selected in GA yields different estimation results. The performance comparison among different OFs are investigated in detail, based on which, an optimal OF is suggested according to the specific requirements. To assure the reliability of estimated results, the scattered waves by target to be matched are computed by the full wave numerical method.

articleTitle: Broadband filtering dielectric resonator antenna with harmonic suppression
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A broadband, low profile and high gain filtering dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is investigated in this paper. Four resonant modes are simultaneously excited in the DRA to provide a broad bandwidth of 59.6% and an average gain of 9.42 dBi within passband, while a shorting via and two pairs of transverse stubs are introduced into the feeding mircostrip line to generate radiation nulls in stopband and obtain filtering characteristic. Second harmonic suppression has been achieved without increasing the footprint of the antenna, and an out-of band suppression of more than 20 dB is obtained within the wide stopband.

articleTitle: EM-driven multi-objective design of impedance transformers by pareto ranking bisection algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In the paper, the problem of fast multi-objective optimization of compact impedance matching transformers is addressed by utilizing a novel Pareto ranking bisection algorithm. It approximates the Pareto front by dividing line segments connecting the designs found in the previous iterations, and refining the obtained candidate solutions by means of poll-type search involving Pareto ranking. The final Pareto set is obtained using surrogate-based optimization techniques. Our approach is validated using a compact impedance matching transformer and compared to state-of-the-art surrogate-assisted techniques.

articleTitle: Wireless energy harvesting using a negatively charged UV antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Positively charged air particles are harmful to health. This paper proposes the use of negatively charged UV antenna to neutralize the positively charged pollutants into a DC electricity without any external power supply. The UV antenna is negatively charged by a natural source of negative ions. The output voltage reflects on the density of the atmospheric positive ions. The proposed system generates 0.42 V in the absence of an UV light if the antenna is connected to the negative ion source. On exposure to an UV light, the proposed system generates 0.55 V. Without the negative ion source, however, the output voltage fell to around 10 mV and no significant voltage rise can be observed even in the presence of an UV light.

Author Keywords: Surface Plasmonic Resonance. Kelvin Water Dropper

articleTitle: A structure and design optimization of compact antenna for Internet of Things applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A compact wideband monopole antenna is proposed for IoT applications. The antenna consists of a microstrip feed line, a rectangular radiator and a ground plane. The main objective is to achieve a small size of the antenna by numerical optimization of all antenna parameters while maintaining the electrical characteristic of antenna at the acceptable level. The antenna design exhibits dimensions of only 3.7 mm × 11.8 mm and the footprint of 44 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Simulation results are validated through measurements of the fabricated antenna prototype.

articleTitle: Fast electric-field integral-equation solver for the multiple right-hand-side problems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Iterative solution of the electric-field integral-equation (EFIE) faces redundant computations for the multiple right-hand-side (RHS) problems. An efficient direct solver of the EFIE based on hierarchically compressed matrix algorithm is developed to deal with multiple RHSs. The multilevel UV method is employed to construct a hierarchically compressed matrix. Exploiting the symmetry of EFIE system matrix, a hierarchical LDL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup> decomposition algorithm is introduced to further reduce the computational costs. A representative application of the analysis of monostatic radar cross section (RCS) is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The application of multi-component LFM signals to radar detection of plasma-covered reentry object
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we utilized multi-component LFM signal as radar transmitted signal to deal with the problem of radar detection of plasma-covered reentry object. By proper design of the multi-component LFM signal combined with the crossing point detection in ambiguity function of echo signal, one can reduce the plasma effect significantly in radar detection.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized microstrip antenna with high isolation and UWB
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This letter presents a planar dual-polarized patch antenna with Ultra-wideband (UWB) technologies and high port isolation. Each port of proposed antenna is mainly composed of a monopole and a feed line. They are used for obtaining UWB characteristic and generating two orthogonal polarization modes. Furthermore, the impedance matching can be attained through etching slots on the ground plane. A cross-polarization ratio of 32 dB on the xoz-plane, 29dB on yoz-plane for port 1, and a cross-polarization ratio of 37 dB on the xoz-plane, 41 dB on the yoz-plane. The isolation is 25 dB over the whole operating band and UWB is from 5.4 to 8.3GHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable frequency selective surface radome for tunable antenna RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable frequency selective surface (FSS) using varactor diodes is presented for low RCS radome application. The FSS is composed of three-layered metallic structures. The varactors are biased with a middle layer bias wire connected to via holes and wire grids on front layer. The back layer is a wideband bandstop structure for out-of-band RCS reduction. The FSS radome without back layer is fabricated and test. Full-wave simulations show the designed FSS radome with back layer has a tuning range from 2.3 GHz to 3.5 GHz with an transmission lower than -10 dB within the X and Ku band.

articleTitle: An IR-UWB indoor positioning based on TOA and band-gap modulations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An IR-UWB indoor positioning is proposed in the paper that combines the algorithm of Time-of-Arrival (TOA) and band-gap modulations. The positioning is referenced by three UWB locators that have different band-gap and deployed in a right triangle. An object can determine its position by identifying pulse backscattered on locators and each locator's signatures through recognizing the exact segment of band-gap and the time of arrival. This positioning scheme is validated by a scenario where the object for positioning is placed at the coordinate of (60.00 mm, 80.00 mm) and band-gaps for three locators are 5.00GHz, 6.50GHz and 7.25GHz. Simulation results show the object is positioned at the coordinate of (60.98mm, 82.77mm), a deviation about 0.98mm in horizontal direction (x axial) and 2.77mm in vertical(y axial).

articleTitle: Active millimeter wave imaging system with sparse antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An active millimeter wave imaging system with sparse antenna array for security inspection is introduced in this review. Several key parts and related techniques of the imaging system are explained and numerical results are provided.

articleTitle: Mid-range wireless power transfer to multiple small receivers using metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the characteristics of a printable mid-range one transmitter coil to four small receiver coils wireless power transfer (WPT) system. The size of the transmitter coil is 40.4cm ×40.4cm × 2mm. The four receiver coils is identical and each one has the size of the 13.6cm × 13. 6cm × 1mm. The spacing distance is 80cm between the transmit coil to the surface of the four receiver coils. Note that it must be a low efficiency magnetic resonate system due to the bigger spacing distance compared to the size of both the transmitter and receivers. Therefore, a metasurface is proposed and integrated with the WPT system to enhance the transfer efficiency. The simulation results show that the total efficiency can be as high as 92% when all parts of the system are put on the optimized position.

articleTitle: FPGA-based control module for millimeter wave imaging system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Design of a control module for millimeter wave imaging system based on FPGA is presented in this paper. There are four parts in the module: scanning control module of antenna array, data acquisition and storage control module, ethernet transmission control module and mechanical scanning platform control module.

articleTitle: An automatic registration method for SAR and optical images based on line extraction and control points selection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Comprehensive utilization of SAR image and optical satellite photograph is a vital yet challenging task in remote sensing detection field. For this purpose, multisensory image registration is a conceivable approach. This paper presents an automatic registration method for SAR and optical images based on line extraction and control points selection. To begin with, line extraction is implemented with Gaussian-gamma-shaped (GGS) bi-windows and Line Segment Detection (LSD) methods, followed by coarse and fine registration. The coarse registration provides matched control point candidates for the subsequent refined registration to improve precision. Adequately considering individual features of SAR and optical images and advantages of processing algorithms corresponding to them, this method can provide enough and unambiguous information for comprehensive utilization of SAR and optical images.

articleTitle: Electro-thermal simulation of graphene nanoribbon interconnects
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The electro-thermal simulation of graphene nanoribbon (GNR) interconnects is presented in this paper. The Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) is solved under the relaxation time approximation (RTA). The power density, which is obtained by the Boltzmann-Poisson approach, is used as the Joule-heating source in heat conduction equation to calculate the temperature profile along the GNR. The result is then sent back to the BTE for updating the distribution function. This process is iterated until self-consistency is achieved. Based on this method, the current-voltage characteristics of metallic GNRs with different lengths and bias conditions are investigated.

articleTitle: Prediction model of dual-frequency in-band electromagnetic radiation effects for electronic equipment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: According to the insufficient research on the complex electromagnetic environment adaptability for the electronic equipment, two kinds of prediction model for dual-frequency in-band electromagnetic radiation effects is established. The decision method of choosing prediction model for electronic equipment is put forward. The ultra-short wave communication stations are selected as equipment under test. The test results verify the validity of the prediction model for dual-frequency in-band electromagnetic radiation effects.

articleTitle: Decoupling multi-element patch arrays using waveguided band-gap structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An efficient approach to suppress the mutual coupling of a three-element microstrip patch array and a four-element microstrip patch array is proposed using waveguided band-gap structure (WG-BGS). The waveguided band-gap structure are realized by crossed-meander-line slits, which exhibit band-gap property. By inserting the WG-BGS between the elements of coupled patch arrays, the mutual coupling of the three-element patch array has been reduced effectively within the -10dB bandwidth (from 3.43 to 3.58GHz), and a maximum value of 13dB has been achieved at 3.5GHz. The mutual coupling of the four-element patch array has been reduced effectively within the -10dB bandwidth (from 3.43 to 3.57GHz), and a maximum value of 11dB has been also achieved at 3.5GHz.

articleTitle: High resolution process based on interpolation and extrapolation in random step frequency radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel method for improving the range-velocity resolution is developed in random step radar. With the interpolation and extrapolation (IE), the range sidelobe caused by the discontinuous spectra and frequencies hopping can be suppressed significantly. The velocity resolution can be improved by IE algorithm in the same way. Finally the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimal design of uniformly excited concentric ring arrays with the reduced number of elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for the optimal design of sparse concentric ring arrays (CRA) is proposed. Owing to the property of Bessel function, the synthesis of CRA can be recast as a sparse constrained approximation problem and solved with compressive sensing method. A representative numerical experiment is provided to assess the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method in comparison with the state-of-the-art synthesis algorithm.

articleTitle: Low-complexity non-uniform diagonal loading for robust adaptive beamforming
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a low-complexity robust adaptive beamforming method is proposed to against array steering vector (ASV) mismatch and effects of low snapshots. The robustness of proposed method depends on two aspects: the non-uniform diagonal loading which prevent the beamformer weight vector from converging to the noise components and variable diagonal loading factor can be changed adaptively when the input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) changed. Simulations results demonstrate that the proposed method provides strong robustness against ASV mismatch and effects of low number of snapshots.

articleTitle: A novel circularly polarized microstrip antenna with a circular slot
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel circularly polarized microstrip slot antenna is designed in this paper. The circularly polarized radiation is generated by the use of annular grooved tandem coupling on the ground plane. The feeder network consists of a microstrip line and a cross-shaped patche. According to the simulation results of HFSS software, the relative bandwidth reaches 4.8%. The proposed antenna has the characteristics of simple structure, miniaturization and excellent performance.

articleTitle: Design of two-turns loop antenna with magnetic core for efficient wireless powering of medical telemetry
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present an inductive powering system of a two-turns loop antenna which includes external and implanted antennas each with a cylinder magnetic core. It can wirelessly transfer power to loop antenna of a compact plane structure in cortex. Compared to single antenna without magnetic core, it can achieve highly-efficient (24.8%) wireless power transferring to implanted loop antenna and reduce the SAR to 83.2%. By improving the link power transfer efficiency and decreasing the SAR, we optimize the antenna's structural parameter. Then, we propose different liquid of concentrations to simulate human skin, which is used for power transmission experiment at 100MHz.

articleTitle: On the correction of the radiation fields solving of phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The field strength correction mechanism of radiation fields of phased array antennas solving by the approximate superposition method is analyzed. When approximate superposition method is used to achieve radiation fields of phased array antennas accurately, the fields must be corrected according to the power. The field strength correction coefficients depend on the array elements numbers, interval of elements, the beam direction of antennas, etc.

articleTitle: A fast algorithm for modeling quasi-periodic arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Many electromagnetic devices, such as metasurfaces, reflectarray antennas, nano particle arrays, can be modeled as quasi-periodic arrays. Simulation of electromagnetic wave interaction with such arrays are very challenging because they are usually large multi-scale models. In this work, we develop a fast algorithm to model quasi-periodic arrays. In this algorithm, we take advantage of the similarities among elements and apply reduced basis method to construct a small basis set for elements. The periodic location of element allows us to apply fast Fourier transform to further accelerate the computation. Numerical example demonstrates that this method has potential in solving larger scale quasi-periodic arrays.

articleTitle: Efficient generation of 3-d capacitance macromodel based on finite difference method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Capacitance macromodel is a novel idea recently proposed for encrypting sensitive structures and bringing acceleration in the capacitance extraction of integrated circuits. The existing technique of macromodeling employs boundary element method (BEM), but may lead to unreliable results due to computational error. In this work, we present the technique of generating the capacitance macromodel based on finite difference method (FDM). Numerical experiments with three-dimensional (3-D) structures show the FDM based technique is more reliable and efficient than BEM. And, the obtained capacitance matrix well satisfies the requirement for using the macromodel-aware floating random walk method in capacitance extraction.

articleTitle: Improvement of microwave heating uniformity via shelled processing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As an efficient and clean energy, microwaves have been widely used for industrial production. However, hot spots and thermal runaway have prevented the large-scale application of microwaves. In this paper, a new multiphysics model is proposed to solve the problem of non-uniform heating. In this model, electromagnetics and heat transfer are coupled to simulate the heating process. The sample is wrapped by shells in order to get more uniform electric filed distribution. The heating uniformities of shelled and non-shelled samples are discussed by considering different sizes of samples and shells. The results show that the shelled processing can obviously improve the heating uniformity of microwaves.

articleTitle: Coupled-mode analysis for modal birefringence of high-order modes in geometry-perturbed fibers
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Modal birefringence of the high-order modes in geometry-perturbed fibers with a multiple rotational symmetry core is analyzed by coupled-mode theory. The criterion of modal birefringence is thus identified by the angular-matching condition in mode couplings, which can be verified by waveguide modal analysis. It will benefit for the applications of the kind of fibers.

articleTitle: A novel wideband metamaterial absorber for antenna RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel double-layer wideband metamaterial absorber (MA) is proposed and applied to a broadband aperture coupling patch antenna. In order to broaden the bandwidth in MA, bulkier and cheaper substrates are required, resulting in the selection of a dielectric substrate on an air substrate. Then the proposed MA is conformal to an aperture coupling patch antenna to reduce RCS of the antenna. The simulated results indicate that the proposed MA-based antenna processes a remarkable RCS reduction from 3GHz to 15.8 GHz for the both polarization, with a maximum reduction of 21.9 dB under x-polarization incidence and 22.6 dB under y-polarization incidence at 8.7GHz. The operation band of the proposed antenna is also covered by the reduction band, which is from 8.1GHz to 10.9GHz.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit analysis of a broadband reflectarray element for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An equivalent circuit model for a multiple resonance reflectarray element is presents in this study. It allows predicting the broadband characteristics of the element from only a few full wave simulations. The equivalent circuit approach can provide good insight into the physical and design properties of periodic structure.

articleTitle: Design of an infrared absorber based on resistance frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Infrared stealth is increasingly important in modern war, for active infrared detection the stealth material should perform high absorption. An infrared absorber which consists of a metal ground plane, a dielectric slab and resistance patches is designed based on the resistance frequency selective surface (RFSS). The absorption of the absorber is investigated by the CST Microwave Studio and the simulation results show that the absorption of the absorber in a wavelength range of both 3-5 μm and 8-12 μm is greater than 90%.

articleTitle: Dual-frequency linear-to-circular polarization converter with half transmission and half reflection based on SRR coupling metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A dual-frequency linear-to-circular polarization converter with half transmission and half reflection is designed using a single-layered metamaterial composed of coupled split ring resonators(SRRs) in this paper. The unit cell of this metamaterial structure include two pairs of coupled SRRs of different sizes, and is periodically arranged in plane. The simulated results show that the metamaterial designed can realize linear-to-circular polarization conversion and half transmission and half reflection at 4.34GHz and 5.97GHz simultaneously.

articleTitle: A lightweight and low-cost 3D printed waveguide for medium power applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A class of 3D printed waveguide structures is presented based on the epoxy coating. An arbitrary 3D structure of a waveguide system is designed and fabricated by 3D printing technique. Then, the whole structure is dipped into a low viscosity solution of silver epoxy and Isopropanol in order to coat a conductor layer on the inner surfaces of the waveguides. The ordinary coaxial cables are used to feed the system. As an example, the coaxial to waveguide adapter as a main building block of most waveguide systems are fabricated in the X-band and measured in a back-to-back setup. In comparison with the conventional metal waveguides, the loss is slightly higher but the weight and cost of are much less.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of charging characteristics of spacecraft dielectric materials
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to study the charging characteristics of aerospace dielectric materials and analyze the influence of the material thickness on the equilibrium potential and the charging time, the differential equation of the surface potential is obtained. The charging expression of the ground simulation space charged process can be attained by solving the differential equation, the simulation curves comparing with the measured data. The charging model of the dielectric material is established, and the correctness of the model is verified. Meanwhile, the relationship between the surface potential of the spacecraft and the thickness of the material is obtained by model programming. At last, verification of the model indicates that the charging discipline of the dielectric material is obtained, which solve the problem of time consuming charging experiment, saving the experimental cost, the simulation results having certain guiding significance for the selection of spacecraft dielectric materials and electrostatic protection of space equipment.

articleTitle: Accelerated computing FDTD algorithm based on lossy dispersion medium
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to reduce the consumed run time and enhance the calculation efficiency for analyzing the propagation properties of an underwater low-frequency electromagnetic wave, a novel approach of modelling the sea with a lossy Drude dispersive medium is proposed. The numerical results of three cases verify the accuracy and validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Beam wander of Bessel-Gaussian beams in non-Kolmogorov turbulent atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We analyze the influences of non-Kolmogorov turbulence and source parameters on beam wander of Bessel-Gaussian (BG) beams in the atmosphere. BG vortex beams with larger topological charge and beam parameter η can better mitigate the turbulence effects on beam wander than BG non-vortex beams. Both inner- and outer-scale effects on beam wander should be considered when BG beam goes through atmosphere. The inner-scale effects on the beam wander are larger than the outer-scale effects.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of electromagnetic environment for shipboard equipment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the modeling and simulation of the electromagnetic environment of shipboard equipment is studied. The electromagnetic environment simulation of the ship is carried out on the basis of establishing the sea surface and the ship model and under the different electromagnetic physical quantity. Sea and ship models will be drawn by CAD software, obtaining the electromagnetic simulation results through the Ship EDF platform. The simulation results are the electric field intensity distribution and ship surface current distribution. Finally, comparing the electric field distribution under different field intensity and the ship surface current distribution under different frequencies, the characteristics of ship electromagnetic environment are received.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from two-dimensional nonlinear rough sea surfaces under circularly polarized wave incidence
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Under circularly polarized wave incidence, the influence of sea surface nonlinear interactions on electromagnetic scattering signatures is studied by utilizing the polarimetric scattering model of second-order small-slope approximation (SSA-II) combined with “choppy wave” model (CWM) for describing nonlinear hydrodynamic interactions between ocean waves. Analogous to linear polarization case, numerical simulations show that under circularly polarized wave incidence nonlinear hydrodynamic interactions between ocean waves also have significant impacts on electromagnetic scattering signatures of radar sea-echo for large incidence angles, in particular at low-grazing angles.

articleTitle: Synthesis of dispersionless zero group delay line for series-fed antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Series-fed antenna arrays always experienced beam-squinting issue. Zero group delay(ZGD) element providing a potential solution for squint-free beamforming in series-fed antenna arrays. In this paper a novel synthesis approach for dispesionless optimized zero group delay line is proposed for the first time. Polynomial synthesis based approach is adopted which provides more design flexibility. Complete design steps followed by a synthesis example of flat magnitude and ZGD responses is presented. The exact agreement between the polynomial and coupling matrix based responses validate the proposed synthesis method.

articleTitle: Bi-mode active frequency selective surface working at 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A bi-mode active frequency selective surface (AFSS) switching between band-pass and band-stop modes is presented in this paper. For large scale application, a novel bias network based on Wheatstone bridge is adopted in design. The good performance of AFSS proves its potentials in improving the security of indoor communication.

articleTitle: Improving the radiation performance of pyramidal horn antennas using a metasurface lens
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a convenient approach to control the electromagnetic waves inside horn antennas to improve their radiation performance by placing a metasurface lens inside the horn. The lens consists of two identical metallic dipole arrays printed on both sides of a single dielectric layer. Through full-wave electromagnetic simulations, a comparative study of the enhanced radiation properties of a standard pyramidal horn loaded by a metasurface lens is conducted. Compared with the original air-filled horn antenna, the metasurface horn produces a 30 dB sidelobe reduction in the E plane.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Dali Lake based on Sentinel-1 data
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The inland lake is an important part of water supplies in arid areas, which is highly sensitive to the changes of hydrological environment and human activities. Lakes located in the arid environment are more sensitive to human activities and climate changes than in other regions. Dali Lake, the important lake in the arid areas of Inner Mongolia, has important index significance. In this paper, an effective method of filtering enhancement with threshold method was developed for rapid extraction and change detection of Dali Lake by using the Sentinel-1 SAR images since 2015. This research provides a reference for further research on lakes in the inland arid area using Sentinel-1 satellite data.

articleTitle: A novel ray tracing method of creeping waves on triangular mesh surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The main problem in calculating the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) surface diffracted fields on surfaces lies in the difficulty in determining the geodesic paths which the creeping rays propagate along. In this paper, a novel adaptation normal-section tracing algorithm (ANST) is presented for creeping ray tracing on the arbitrarily shaped surfaces modeled by triangular surfaces. The proposed creeping ray tracing algorithm is efficient and accurate for ray tracing on arbitrarily shaped complex shapes. The validity and efficiency of the algorithm is verified by analytical and measurement results.

articleTitle: An efficient solution method for nonlinear analysis of microwave amplifier circuit
